The add itself: a same-direction 30m STRAT 2-2 trigger inside the 30m bar where a winning 15m 2-2 (with 1D+1h continuity) hit its magnitude target. 30m stop and magnitude target, 5h hold. Result -0.007R [-0.034, +0.021] vs matched control. Powered NULL. Only the 15m-to-30m rung was tested.

Gate on the phase-3 5m CISD book (2R, 50 min): keep trades whose target distance is at most 1.3x the ADR the day has left (126-day ADR). Gated 71k trades vs 22k complement: -0.005R [-0.022, +0.011]. Powered NULL.

'Beyond the ADR means reversal': fade the extension at the first M1 close each day where the day's range reaches the ADR (stop 0.25 ADR, 1R, 4h, control matched on time of day). Result +0.020R [-0.038, +0.080] vs matched random entries. Powered NULL.
Refuted (faithfulness): any 3-bar swing does better (+0.023R); the faithful reading b is NULL.
Same book as reading a, but the ITH bar must sweep the prior STH (trade above it, then close back below it), as in the narrated chart procedure. Powered NULL (+0.008R).

15m closes through a 2/2 STH/STL, entered at the open after the 4-candle window, stop at the 50% retracement of the leg, 1R. Gate = aggressive by the threshold_fits magnitude test (1.5/0.65), which passed on 41% of breaks. Aggressive breaks do not retrace less. Powered NULL.

Candle-3 stack gate (last closed daily AND last closed 4H bar are C2s in the trade direction) on the 15m rung-0 CISD book. Gated 1,998 vs complement 30,731: +0.001R [-0.051,+0.055]. Powered null.

Live expansion-support gate: the in-progress daily and 4H candles are both beyond their open in the trade direction, with opposing run <= 1.0 x body. Tested on the 15m CISD book: +0.008R [-0.021,+0.038]. Powered null.

Daily C2, protected swing taken from the latest same-direction 1h CISD inside the C2 and still intact at the close. Entry at the 18:00 Asia open, stop at the swing, target the C2's bias-side extreme, held one session. Diff about 0; MDE 0.114.
Autobias 1: 5m CISD setups that agree with the last 4H (forex grid) C2 closure direction, compared with the setups it suppresses. A powered zero.
Autobias 2: the same book gated on agreement with the last daily C2 closure direction. A powered zero.

Pooled auto rungs: 1h CISD with 1D, 15m with 4H (forex grid), 5m with 1H. Gated = the last completed auto-paired HTF bar is a candle 2 in the event's direction. Result +0.008R, powered NULL (MDE 0.023).
Refuted (both): the 'range covered' complement is a late-session set; ToD-matched control gives NULL (+0.024 [-0.010,+0.057]).
Refuted (both): same time-of-day confound as reading a; NULL under the ToD-matched control.

Gate on the 15m CISD book: 2R target inside the remaining expansion-day budget (running day low/high plus the expansion band) vs beyond it: +0.018R, a powered NULL (H1 +0.041, H2 -0.003). A target ceiling adds nothing beyond the 'range already covered' gate.

Corollary 'after a very large range day (>1.5x ADR20) expect a smaller range': the next day's range was below ADR only 43% of the time vs 56% on matched random days. NEGATIVE: volatility clusters, and big days are followed by big days.

The data has no volume, so the balance area is a time-at-price (TPO) stand-in: the previous day's 70% value area and point of control (POC). Event: the first M1 close back inside after closing outside.
Verifiers upheld (+0.024R, independent build identical) but H2 +0.0006 and BH q=0.11 - candidate only.
Premium/discount rule (longs below the previous day's EQ, shorts above) as a gate on the reading-a BPR book: +0.033R, CI contains 0, powered NULL.

Clustered by gap. Powered NULL: BPR revisits are no better. The untouched-gap arm itself beat its own control by +0.033R.

Tested the running expectation 'after a higher low comes a higher high' on 1h 2/2 fractals. At a confirmed higher low inside an HH/HL trend, go long with the stop at the HL and the target at the pending prior swing high, 24 trading hours (mirror for downtrends). -0.047R vs control, powered NULL.

Gate test of the conservative variant: take HTF-bias entries only after the opposite 1h swing liquidity is grabbed. Baseline is 1h closes the day after a daily C2/C3+H1-CISD bias. +0.14R [-0.0001,+0.29], MDE 0.21, UNDERPOWERED. H1 +0.36 and H2 -0.10 disagree.

Earlier 'catch them right away' reading (E6bpY4dQvlE): the same setups entered at the close back inside the range. NULL.

An execution-quality claim (a stop order may not fill at its level). Testing it needs broker fill records or bid/ask ticks. The dataset is a mid-quote M1 OHLC series, and the harness always fills stops at the stop level or the gap open.

When a 15m CISD 2R position reaches +1R and then returns to entry, holding on with the original stop and target vs a matched random entry: +0.036R, NULL (powered, MDE 0.062). The return to entry predicts neither failure nor success, so break-even vs a structural stop is a wash.
Refuted (both): nearest-neighbour null has a far-tail boundary bias; placebo blocks give the same effect and a 20-bar lookback kills it.
Refuted (faithfulness): a placebo without the breaker's higher high gives the same edge; 2021 alone carries 37%.
Host's hard requirement of a higher-timeframe bias, tested as a gate on the breaker book: direction agrees with the daily previous-candle bias. -0.044R (wrong sign), CI contains 0, underpowered.

15m breaker continuation: swing low L1, then swing high H, then L1 swept before any close above H, then a close above H within 20 bars. Traded only with the prior day's direction. Entry at the close through H, stop on the swept low, 2R. No better than a matched random entry (powered, MDE 0.037).

Same breakers, entered on a retest instead: the first bar within 10 bars that trades into the body zone and closes beyond its far side, with the stop on that far side and a 2R target. Zero difference from a matched random entry (powered, MDE 0.065).

Gate on the 5m breaker-retest book (27,065 filled): limit at the breaker's near edge, stop at its far edge, 2R, 50 min hold. Gated = wick-only breakers, meaning no 5m body closed beyond L1 during the lower-low leg (8,234), vs body-violated (18,823). Powered NULL (MDE 0.054).

The harness cannot move a stop mid-trade, so the trail was tested as the position it leaves. That position starts at the first later same-direction 1h CISD while the base trade (prior-day target at least 2R away) is still open.

Later framing (prior-day range / outside bar): after PDH or PDL is taken and a 1H bar closes back inside, the other side is reached before the 17:00 NY halt 15.0% of the time. The matched null (same distance, same M1-bar horizon, same time of day) reaches it 16.2%. NULL, powered.

Earlier framing (a range between 1H swings): a swing is taken and a 1H bar closes back inside within 3 bars, then the opposite swing is reached within 1,440 M1 bars 53.7% of the time, against 54.6% for the matched null. NULL, powered.

Range = the previous day. When a 15m candle closes back inside after a failed run through PDH or PDL, the opposite side is hit within 12 trading hours 11.0% of the time, against 11.4% for a level at the same distance and time of day. This is a powered NULL.

Tested whether a fresh 15m fractal-2/2 swing pool gets traded through within 360 M1 bars more often than a same-distance level at a matched random time: 69.8% vs 69.5%, a powered NULL. The first run's write was refused on params_source keys and the deterministic test was re-run once, with identical numbers;

Tested sweep-and-reject of untaken 15m pools, trading toward the nearest opposite pool with the stop at the sweep bar's extreme (6h hold, trading time, ToD-matched control). Diff +0.115R but MDE 0.28R: the stop is tight and the target far, so R is heavy-tailed. UNDERPOWERED.

Baseline is the minimal-confirmation 4h C2 plus 15m CISD book. Gate is a proxy for 'strong structure', declared before the run: C1 is a clean small-wick expansion (opposing run / body <= 1.0) and C2 closes through the open of the HTF opposing series. It fired on 8.2% of events. Result: -0.020R [-0.101, +0.060].

Setup: a 1h C2 sweeps the previous hour's extreme into a POI (PDL/PWL, session levels, 1h swings, 1h FVGs). A 5m unicorn (breaker plus an overlapping FVG, within 12 candles) forms inside C2 and the trade is taken there. Stop at the C2 extreme, 2R, 4h hold. -0.044R vs control, CI [-0.132, +0.046].

Inside the 4H C2 model (one-sided C2 on the forex grid, plus an aligned 15m CISD inside C2), C3 entries with an intracandle CISD were compared with all other C3/C4 model entries, clustered by C2. They are not better (powered, MDE 0.073). Scored on control-adjusted R, not raw win rate.

Gate on Trader T's book with no cancel rule: fills before the 2R price traded (86.6%) vs fills after price had already run to the target. Difference +0.0005R, essentially zero. UNDERPOWERED because the cancelled arm is small (546; MDE 0.235).

Variant B on 4H (forex grid) and 1D: C2 takes C1's extreme and closes beyond it, then C3 closes through the series open (a CISD). Entry at the C3 close, stop at the C2/C3 extreme, 2R. Diff +0.036R, CI [-0.059, +0.125]; MDE 0.131, so it is short of power.

Variant A: a lower-timeframe CISD (4H with 15m, 1D with 1H) inside an unfinished HTF C2 whose swing is beyond C1's extreme. Stop at the protected swing, 2R. Diff +0.002R, CI [-0.020, +0.024]. Powered NULL.

Baseline: 16,184 4h candles (forex grid), each traded in its close direction from the next open with ±1 ATR(20) barriers and a 3-candle hold in trading time. Gate: body at least as large as the opposing run, i.e. not a reversal candle (fires 64.8%). -0.009R, CI [-0.040, +0.021].

UNTESTABLE. Chooses between vehicles: futures chart vs ETF/options/CFD, minis vs micros. Only one instrument series exists (spot gold, already including overnight), so there is no second vehicle to compare levels, signals or fills against.

Gate test of the indicator's session filter. The concept's own video gives no bounds, so it uses the same indicator's stated 8-11 EST setting from Je7cd9HJUBE, read on the New York clock with DST. Run on the 5m CISD book: +0.005R [-0.017,+0.027]. A powered NULL.

Deep dive: a structural control (stop at a fresh 15m extreme, same distance) removes 60-85% of +0.078R; residual +0.02-0.03R, negative in 2024; median stop 0.435pt so a 0.30pt spread nets -2.3R/trade. Not tradeable.

15m CISD by his definition (close past the first candle's open, POI gate on, 2/2 swing, max_wait 3), stop at the protected swing, 2R, 150min, against a matched control: -0.007R, a powered NULL (MDE 0.019).
Same book, but the close must clear the whole series' far extreme (the wording in hourly-cisd-confirmation): -0.008R, a powered NULL.

15m model: sweep of the prior 20-bar range, CISD back inside, limit-style entry on a retest of the CISD level within 150 min, premium/discount filter. Stop at the manipulation extreme, target the -2 SD projection (2R). Powered null (MDE 0.057).

Gate on the cisd-a book: kept trades (>=1R of room between the closure and the short-term target, taken as the last confirmed opposite 2/2 swing before the extreme) vs skipped ones gave +0.008R, a powered NULL. The skip condition fired on 88% of CISDs.

Monday or Tuesday daily C2 closure that is the week's extreme, with an hourly CISD inside the day. Enter at the C3 open, stop at the extreme, 2R, hold to Friday 17:00 NY in trading minutes. MDE 0.24, effective n 175.

Full four-part checklist: daily C3, 4H C4, previous-day extreme not yet taken, 15m CISD. Stop at the protected swing, target the previous-day extreme with a 2R floor, hold to the daily close. 174 trades, +0.35R vs control; the CI excludes 0 but the MDE is 0.46, far below the power floor. Candidate only.
Arithmetic reductio with no market claim. Checked: 1%/day gives x10 at 231.4 days, x100 at 462.8, x1000 at 694.2, x10k at 925.6 and x100k at 1157. That matches the quoted ladder from a $1,000 start.

Reading A (a close beyond the CE invalidates the gap). The first CE touch of a 1H FVG closing beyond the CE but inside the gap reaches the far edge within 600 trading minutes 91.2% of the time, against a distance-matched null of 91.0%. The null is not time-of-day matched.

Respect reading: the first CE touch of a 1H FVG closing back on the respecting side reaches the displacement leg's extreme within 600 trading minutes 51.8% of the time, against a null of 52.7%. The null is not time-of-day matched. No continuation edge (powered, MDE 0.021).

Consolidation defined as no 1h close beyond the latest 2/2 swing in the last 24 bars (absence of displacement), used as a gate on the phase-3 1h CISD book, claim '-'. The gate fired on only 0.7% of events (55 of 8,033), so the test cannot decide.

Gate on the 15m bare-CISD book: the last completed daily candle is an inside day. Claim '-' (worse), but gated trades came out 0.044R better, with the CI excluding 0 and both halves positive: NEGATIVE, p=0.021. Unlikely to survive campaign-wide Holm.

Gate on the 15m bare-CISD book: the last three completed 4H closes (forex grid) all sit inside the range of the 4H candle before them. Claim '-', but gated trades came out 0.041R better: NEGATIVE, p=0.013. Correlated with reading a.

Faded the first 1H run of a mother-candle high or low when the prior days were all inside days and the run bar closed back inside. Stop at the run extreme, target the opposite external level, 24h trading-time hold.

On no-bias days (prior daily candle neither C2 nor C3), the nearer 18:00-09:30 range extreme is taken first 60.7% of the time vs a 60.0% geometry-matched null at the same clock. Nearness explains it all.
The rotation claim, that both pre-open extremes are taken 09:30-16:00 on no-bias days: 5.9% vs 8.2% for the matched null. Rotation is rarer than chance, the opposite of what the concept claims.

Range = a 1h mother bar plus 3 inside bars. The side taken first sets the direction; entry on a 5m close back inside the range, stop at the sweep extreme, target the opposite side. 2,184 trades at +0.02R versus control. The 18% win rate makes the R variance large, giving an MDE of 0.22R.

Reading b: the bias selects which side must be run. Tested as a gate on the reading-a book: trades aligned with the daily previous-candle bias versus the rest. 756 aligned trades at -0.17R, against the claim, but the CI is wide (MDE 0.45R).

Event: any of the three triggers fires (first take of the prior week's high or low this week; overextension; close at the EQ of the dealing range). The next day is a consolidation day (|close-open| <= 0.2 ADR20) 28.5% of the time vs a 27.8% regime-matched base rate: +0.7pp, CI [-2.0, +3.3]pp. Powered, so NULL.

Gate on the 15m CISD book. 'Consolidating' means a completed day's range contains the 2 or more real days after it (inside-days box, searching back up to 20 days) and today has not yet taken either side of it; about 8% of entries. Outside vs inside: +0.006R, CI [-0.041, +0.052]. Powered, so NULL.

Same gate with the 'small days, small bodies' box: 3 real days, each with range < ADR20 and body <= 0.5 x range, and today still inside their combined range; about 5% of entries. -0.013R, CI [-0.086, +0.056]. Effective n 179, MDE 0.101, so UNDERPOWERED.

Rate test. During daily consolidation (5-day mean range < 0.8x the prior 20 days, bodies < 0.5x range), an alert sits above the top of the nearest open bearish daily FVG above price. When it fires, the nearest unbroken daily swing high was hit within 5 sessions 33.3% of the time vs 39.4% for the matched null.

AM Trades reading. Setup: a Mon-Wed consolidation (no daily close beyond the prior day's range), then Thursday sweeps one side of the Mon-Wed external range, closes back inside and prints a 1h CISD. Trade on Friday: stop at Thursday's extreme, target the far side of the range.

McJflkKuvrI variant. Thursday must take out both Monday's and Wednesday's extreme and close back beyond both; the 1h CISD and Friday trade are the same as reading a. Only 16 setups, below the n>=30 floor, so the harness labels it UNTESTABLE for sample size.

trade_test. Range: 8 x 30m candles spanning <=1.5 ATR. A 5m sweep of one extreme, landing inside an unmitigated same-direction 1H FVG, then a 5m CISD within 2h. Stop at the swept extreme, target the opposite range extreme. Result +0.155R vs control, CI contains 0, MDE 0.25 (n=370).

Claim: a failed closure through the opposing series (no series_open close within 3 1h bars) means the swing extreme is taken before the far side of the range. Hit rate 56.4% against a geometry-matched null of 55.8%, diff +0.7pp. The test is powered (MDE 2.3pp), so this is a well-powered zero.

Half-candle timing rider: on the phase-3 1h CISD book, closures whose first M1 close-through comes in the first half of the confirming candle versus later ones (claim '+'). Timely closures are -0.068R, against the claim (p=0.07). Both halves are negative.

Gate on 15m POI-on CISD closures allowed up to 40 bars late: fast (V-shaped, within 3 bars) closures vs slow ones (which the concept calls consolidation sweeps) gave -0.010R, a powered NULL. Slow closures are not measurably worse.

Gate on the 15m bare-CISD book: the confirming bar also takes out the latest unbroken 2/2 swing extreme. Claim '-'; the difference points the claimed way but the CI contains 0 and the test is powered (MDE 0.041).

Gate on the 15m bare-CISD book: the previous day's high/low objective was already taken before the entry. Claim '-'; the difference points the claimed way but the CI contains 0 and the test is powered (MDE 0.042).

Continuation entry after a confirmed 15m CISD: a same-direction CISD off an FVG tag or swing sweep, with a higher low / lower high and the earlier protected swing intact, entered at market on the closure, stop at the new protected swing, 2R: -0.014R, a powered NULL.

15m CISD book (28,302 events): continuation CISDs (higher low / lower high after a same-direction CISD whose swing held) vs reversal CISDs. -0.004R, CI [-0.032,+0.023], MDE 0.040. Powered null: continuations are no better than reversals.

Setup: a 1H SMT reversal with a swing formed, and the draw (the prior opposite-side swing) still unmet. Trade the first two-stage PSP with the draw inside 24 bars: stop at the reversal extreme, target the draw, 24h hold. Result: +0.043R vs matched control, CI [-0.061, +0.145], MDE 0.147 (n=793 is too few).

Baseline: continuation trades after a 4h (forex grid) expansion candle, with a 2R target and a 40h hold in trading bars. Gate: the next candle is an inside bar, the HTF consolidation signature. 1,527 gated trades at -0.036R; MDE 0.116, just short of power.

Same 4h book. Gate: the next candle closes back inside the expansion candle's range (a small-range consolidation or retracement), versus further expansion or expansion met with expansion. -0.007R; powered, MDE 0.093.

Baseline was 5m CISD in the direction of the prior 1H candle (2R, 50 min hold). Gate: the decision falls in the first 15 minutes of the current 1H candle (time share 0.25). No effect (powered, MDE 0.031).
Speed reading on 15m CISD with max_wait 10. Gate: the close-through lands 3 or fewer bars after the extreme (a fast V), against 4 or more (consolidation). No effect (powered, MDE 0.031).

Gate test on a 1H gold swing-sweep reversal book (9,483 trades). The gate is an SMT against the named gold-triad member XAU/EUR, built from gold and EURUSD H1, and fires on 27% of the book. Gated arm +0.020R vs complement, CI [-0.051, +0.091], MDE 0.102 just above the 0.10 threshold.

Used real CFTC COT data for COMEX gold (088691). At each quarter start: commercial net above the midpoint of its 12-month range = bullish, below = bearish. Gated a daily book with one long and one short every day (1 ATR stop, 2R, one trading day), clustered by quarter. Result: -0.013R, CI [-0.061, +0.036].

Run on M1, because 15-second data does not exist here. A 30-bar up move (1.5x the prior range) stalls at a swing high, then the counter move closes below the leg's internal swing low and leaves an FVG.

Gold 1h CISD, kept when the strength order fits (short gold only when it is weaker than silver since the 18:00 NY open, long only when stronger). Gate = silver swept its 20-bar extreme and closed back inside within the last 3h. Only 395 gated trades (MDE 0.17): UNDERPOWERED.

Same strength-filtered gold 1h CISD book. Gate = a silver 1h CISD in the trade direction within the last 4h. The point estimate is against the claim (-0.065R) but the test is UNDERPOWERED (MDE 0.115).

After gold has already taken its PDH/PDL, silver's first tag of its own PDH/PDL. Trading gold against the move (1 ATR stop, 1R) does worse than the matched control: gold continues rather than turns. The CI upper end sits at -0.002 and p=0.04, so this will not survive Holm.
Silver tags its PDH/PDL while gold has not taken its own (SMT at the level), then gold is traded against the move. Powered, CI contains 0, point estimate negative.

Transfer of the fraction rule to XAUUSD (numerator gold, denominator USD). Book: 1h CISD trades taken opposite a directional dollar, read as inverted EURUSD daily closure. Gate: the gold leg (XAU/EUR line) closed daily in the trade direction, against complement days where that leg was inside or moved with the dollar.

Rauf's variant ranks currency futures (6E, 6B, 6A and so on) by eye and trades the FX pair or cross of the weakest against the strongest. The campaign holds no currency futures or crosses, the harness resolves only XAUUSD, and the grading has no stated measure.

Same-day reversal branch: a 1h CISD whose extreme swept PDH/PDL and is the day's running extreme, first one per day. Stop at the wick, target the opposite previous-day extreme, exit 17:00 NY. NULL, +0.056R, just powered (MDE 0.093).

Next-day bias: a daily C2 or C3 (C2-open reference) closure plus a same-direction H1 CISD gives 867 biased days, matching phase 3's 862. Traded the next session toward D's bias-side extreme with the stop at D's wick. NULL, -0.013R.

Daily C2 sweep-and-close-back, or an inside day read by the order of its extremes (low first then close up, or the mirror), with the read dropped when a contrary 1h CISD sits inside the day. Traded the next session toward the day's bias-side extreme with the stop at the other extreme. Diff about 0;
Previous-candle engine on daily candles (18:00 NY). Trade D+1 toward D's bias-side extreme, stop at D's other extreme, hold one session in bars. Powered NULL, +0.027R.
The same engine run candle by candle on 4H (forex grid), trading the next 4H candle toward the prior candle's bias-side extreme. Well-powered NULL, +0.004R.

Bias-required reading (Ash Trades / $niper). Baseline: phase-3 rung-0 1h CISD book, n=8,030. Gate: trade direction matches the daily bias from the method-spec previous-candle engine on the last completed daily candle. Aligned arm n=3,564; the gate adds +0.040R, CI [-0.017, +0.097]. Powered, so NULL.

Bias-free reading (HolyAngelBruv / DTR): with no daily bias, trade structure breaks. Book: 1h CISD trades taken on no-bias days only. +0.033R vs the matched control, CI [-0.044, +0.118]. Effective n is 295 and MDE 0.116, so UNDERPOWERED.

After a daily C2, buy the first dip below the 18:00 open (before 10:30, still above the previous day's EQ), stop at the EQ, target the previous day's high (mirror for shorts). The difference is negative but the test is underpowered (MDE 0.13).

Gate: among bias-direction 15m CISDs that turn at the day's extreme, keep only those whose extreme formed before 10:30 NY. The gate fires on 93% of trades, so the complement is thin: effective n is 105 and the test is underpowered.

Reading a: a daily FVG counts as inverted when a daily close goes beyond the whole gap. Entry was a kill-zone M1 touch of the level within 5 days, stop at the gap's far side, target the inversion day's extreme. Result -0.17R vs control, CI [-0.41, +0.06]. MDE 0.33 is far above the 0.10 threshold.

Reading b: inversion needs only a daily close beyond the gap's mean threshold. Same kill-zone retest book as reading a. Result -0.17R, CI [-0.42, +0.07]. The sign is negative in both halves but the test is underpowered (about 290 daily events).

Baseline: days that take one side of the previous day, traded in the breach direction at the daily close (1R, one day hold). Gate: the day closed its body through PDH/PDL. The body-close continuation did worse than the wick-only breach, -0.093R, CI [-0.177, -0.011]. That is against the claim, with both halves negative.

Order-of-extremes tie-breaker: on daily closes that land back inside the prior day's range, a high made before the low (on M1) means bearish for the next session, and vice versa. The day's extremes are used as stop and target. Diff -0.003R with CI +/-0.06.

Rule: a doji daily close gives no bias. Tested as a gate (body <= 10% of range, declared before the run) on the previous-candle daily bias book, claim '-'. 174 doji trades at -0.06R, the direction the claim predicts but not significant. n < 200.

Respect rate of the 18:00 session open (later canon). Setup: price moves 0.1x the prior-day range away, then comes back to the open. Respected = +k trades before -k. Null = the same target distances and M1-bar horizon at matched random minutes. 50.6% against 49.9%: the 18:00 open behaves like a random price. Powered.

Same respect test with the midnight open (the earlier recording's reference). 48.7% against a 49.0% geometry-matched null. Neither open acts as support/resistance, and the 18:00-vs-midnight choice makes no difference. Powered.

Event: daily order flow agrees with the nearer objective (an unmitigated daily swing high/low or a live daily FVG). The objective is reached within 5 sessions 69.0% of the time vs a 70.3% geometry-matched null (same distance, same side, same M1 horizon): -1.3pp, CI [-5.1, +2.1]pp.

Tested the claim that expansion never follows expansion. Expansion day = range at least 1.5x a trailing mean that skips the prior day, and opposing run/body at most 1. Measured how often the next day is a same-direction expansion versus a ±21-day random-day null, with claim '-'.

Gate: the profile confirms when the day formed its opposing extreme (opposing run > 0.30 of the running range) and price is now beyond the open in the bias direction. Baseline is 1h closes 03:00-12:00 NY on bias days. +0.105R, CI [-0.061,+0.256], effective n 226, UNDERPOWERED.

Seek & Destroy as a stand-aside day, applied to 15m CISD trades in NY a.m. (08:30-12:00). A day is S&D when London took both Asia extremes. Non-S&D days gave +0.023R. Only about 3% of days are S&D (556 trades in that arm), so the MDE is 0.125: UNDERPOWERED.

London counter-run then New York continuation (the London Reversal and NY Reversal profiles pooled). The gate requires a daily bias, London running counter to it beyond the Asia extreme, no S&D, and a NY entry in the bias direction. Result: +0.003R, MDE 0.113, UNDERPOWERED.
Deep dive: +12.1pp is real but a volatility-only null explains 83% of it; residual +1.8pp decays to +0.2pp in B4. No entry beats a structural control; net -0.08 to -0.38R at 0.30pt.

Gate on the 15m rung-0 CISD book. Blocked trades are entries in the same direction as the day's move once the day's range reaches 80% of the median of the last 3 real days. Kept vs blocked (complement n=4,525): -0.012R, CI [-0.048, +0.021]. Powered (MDE 0.049), so NULL.

Gate test on the sequential 15m bare-CISD book: the first 3 trades of each trading day vs the 4th and later trades the cap rules out. Powered NULL, +0.022R [-0.009, +0.053], MDE 0.044. Re-run twice to fix bugs in _book.py; the notes record both earlier runs, and both were also NULL.

Gate on the batch's 5m unicorn limit book (8,222 trades). Gated = unicorn in the direction of the latest daily C2, its sweep reached the C2's 50% EQ (the only T-spot construction in the corpus: 'just the equilibrium'), and no 1H close has passed the EQ, within 5 days. Only 38 gated trades, so underpowered.

Large daily wick = wick bigger than the body and the other wick. On the next day, entered at the first H1 FVG inside the wick's near half (no H1 close beyond the wick EQ first). Stop at the wick EQ, target the wick day's opposite extreme, 10h hold. Diff was +0.117R, but the test is UNDERPOWERED (n=174, MDE 0.246);

Method 1: a CISD on the session's timeframe (Asia 1h, London 1h/30m/15m, NY 1h/30m/15m/5m) at the day's running extreme, first one per day, traded away from the wick to the previous day's opposite extreme with the exit at 17:00 NY. Powered NULL (MDE 0.080). Re-run once after a same-close tie-ordering fix;

Method 2: a C2 closure (4h in any session, 1h only in NY) at the day's running extreme, same trade. The CI is above 0 and both halves are positive (+0.145 and +0.122), but the verdict is UNDERPOWERED because the MDE is 0.151 against the 0.10 threshold (R variance is high because targets sit far from stops).

Dealing range = the nearest unbroken confirmed 15m swing high and low bounding price, looking back 48 bars. On the 15m rung-0 CISD book, longs in its discount and shorts in its premium show no difference from the rest. Powered, MDE 0.047.
UNTESTABLE because the fib anchors and orientation cannot be recovered: the settings were shown on screen but never read out, so the 0.75 zone cannot be placed.

Transfer from indices to XAU/XAG. Reading a, leader gives back: gold moved at least 1x its typical daily move while silver was flat or opposite. Next session, trade gold against its move, target the day's opposite extreme, stop the other extreme, one session held in bars.

Reading b, laggard catches up: silver is the leader and gold is flat or opposite. Trade gold in silver's direction, target gold's day extreme, stop the other extreme, one session held. 102 events: UNDERPOWERED (+0.08R, MDE 0.61, halves disagree).

15m rung-0 CISD book, NY 08:31-17:00, gated on longs below BOTH the midnight and 08:30 opens (shorts above both). NULL, and it leans against the claim: -0.047R with the CI's upper end at +0.0004. Both halves negative.

Needs footprint / market-delta (aggressor-signed volume). The certified M1 data is OHLC only with no volume column, and OANDA spot gold has no exchange tape, so delta divergence cannot be computed. An OHLC proxy would be testing a different indicator.
Refuted (both): a mirror target at the same distance is hit as often - volatility after a strong close, not continuation.

Same rule with the 4H candle's own close beyond -2.5 as the trigger. The -4 deviation was reached within the next 240 bars 56.6% of the time vs 58.0% for the null. The point estimate is negative and the test is underpowered (MDE 0.070 vs 0.05).

Gate on the $niper prior-day-sweep/MSS/FVG book: limit in the premium/discount half of the MSS leg (sweep extreme to leg extreme) vs the wrong half (53% pass). Result −0.117R, wrong sign, UNDERPOWERED (MDE 0.38, book n=793).
Same $niper book, but the range is the current trading day's running high/low: limit in the correct half vs not (75% pass). Result −0.159R, wrong sign, UNDERPOWERED (MDE 0.40, effective n 202).

Book: 15m closes beyond 2/2 swings, window of 4 bars, stop at the window extreme, 2R, 150min hold. Gate: the threshold_fits magnitude test (range ratio >= 1.5 and distance ratio >= 0.65), which fired on 39% of breaks. +0.015R; powered, MDE 0.048.
Same book. Gate: FVG required, meaning a same-direction 3-bar FVG inside the N=4 window. It fired on 62% of breaks, matching threshold_fits' 61%. +0.011R; powered, MDE 0.051.

Displaced 15m structure break (threshold_fits N=4, 1.5/0.65). A limit at the leg's 0.5 (anchor to the trailed extreme) fills on M1; stop at the anchor, target the trailed leg extreme, 8h exit. No better than the matched random entry. Powered, MDE 0.051.

Each fired 15m displacement leg: limit at the discount FVG (capped at the leg's EQ), stop at the leg start, 2R. The order is re-anchored when the next same-direction leg fires, cancelled on an opposite leg or after 24 bars. The book is every fill. NULL.

The guests' dollar-first gate applied to gold: 1h CISD trades that oppose the dollar, read from the last completed EURUSD weekly candle inverted as a DXY proxy, compared with vetoed trades. Powered NULL, with the point estimate negative.
The FX pair-selection procedure (rank currency futures, trade crosses while the dollar consolidates) needs DXY, currency futures and FX crosses, and the campaign trades only XAUUSD.

3-day stand-aside: 1h CISD entries in the direction of 3 consecutive daily closes beyond the prior day's extreme, vs all other 1h CISD trades, claim '-'. -0.021R with 228 gated trades (2.9%, effective n 125), underpowered.
Refuted (faithfulness): the concept's own condition (late in the expanded candle) carries none of the effect.

Later canon: at the 18:00 NY open the draw is PDH or PDL, picked by the trend in prior-day extremes, with target = the draw and stop = the opposite level for one session. Diff +0.037R. MDE is 0.112 and the effective n of 1107 is below the power floor, so UNDERPOWERED. ctrl_overlap is 38%.

Follow the displacement: yesterday's close vs its open picks PDH or PDL, same bracket as reading a. Diff -0.016R and the CI contains 0. The ToD-matched controls are 49% the concept's own trades (daily 18:00 entries on almost every day), so the harness turned the NULL into UNDERPOWERED.

Driver = the 09:30 NY index open; key levels = PDH/PDL. Branch A (910 trades): if PDL or PDH was swept and reclaimed before 09:30, trade away from it at 09:30. Branch B (35 trades): if neither was touched, fade the first touch of PDH/PDL between 09:30 and 09:45. 2R, exit at 12:00. Powered NULL (MDE 0.089).

Needs a DXY series and a Treasury yield or bond series, and the workspace has neither (only XAU M1 and XAG/EUR H1/D1). The claim is about DXY, not gold, and the source never says whether the bond chart is price or yield, which flips the sign of the divergence.

5m CISD book limited to moments where the pre-open bias (previous daily candle) and the same-day dynamic bias (15m close through a 2/2 swing, with an FVG on the leg) disagree. Trading with the dynamic bias vs the pre-open bias: diff +0.002R, CI [-0.025, +0.029]. Powered NULL; the gate fired on 50% of events.

The ladder can only beat flat 1% sizing if trades after a win do better than trades after a loss, so that is the test (gate: previous taken trade won, claim '+'). Powered NULL, -0.025R [-0.055, +0.006], leaning the wrong way. Sizing off the last outcome adds variance, not expectancy, on this book.
4H/15m: CISDs taken after the 4H C2 closed (continuation in C3) vs early CISDs inside a still-forming 4H C2 gave +0.017R, a powered NULL (MDE 0.061).

Three-tier filter plus the standing rules, on the 15m CISD book. Blocked: Monday sessions, NFP weeks before the 08:30 Friday release, and trades whose hold spans the release. Allowed arm: -0.010R. Powered NULL. NFP is the only calendar used; CPI and FOMC are unmodelled, which attenuates toward 0.

Earlier participation reading: trade only after 08:30 on red-folder days. Baseline is the 15m CISD events from 08:30 to 17:00 NY on Tue-Fri, and the gate is 'NFP day'. +0.027R, but there are only 123 NFP days (effective n below 200, MDE 0.14), so UNDERPOWERED.

Baseline: first-tag reversal trades at a daily FVG, entered on the 4H forex grid (stop beyond the array, 2R, 40h hold in bar time); 439 trades. Gate: the prior day of 4H bars stopped within 0.5 daily ATR of the array and ranged at most 1 daily ATR; it fired on 27%.
Gate test: only taking entries in 08:30-11:00 NY (0bH_kkG2q6s) on the 5m bare-CISD book (98,346 events, 2R, 50 min). Gated minus complement is +0.005R [-0.017,+0.027]. A powered NULL (MDE 0.032).
Gate test: the 09:30-10:00 NY 'opening drive' window (G1IIdQ3RAkY) on the same 5m CISD book. +0.008R [-0.040,+0.059]. A powered NULL (MDE 0.071).

Trade test: a 1H CISD whose protected swing sits in the half of the previous day's range matching its direction (lows in [PDL, EQ] for longs, highs in [EQ, PDH] for shorts). Stop at that swing, target the far side (PDH/PDL) if not yet taken, 10h hold. Result -0.019R [-0.069, +0.033]. Powered, so NULL.

Bias-invalidator reading: the first 1H close through the previous day's EQ, against that day's direction, reaches PDL/PDH by the end of the day 49.6% of the time, against a time-of-day-matched null of 49.3% (powered, MDE 0.039). This is the corrected run.

Expansion-filter reading: 15m CISD trades with the prior 4H candle's direction, gated on the current 4H candle's running extreme having stayed beyond the prior 4H candle's EQ (47% of events pass). Positive but not significant (powered, MDE 0.052).

The device transferred to XAU/XAG because ES and NQ are not in the data. Gold 1h CISD book gated on the prior completed day's ratio candle closing in the trade direction. Gate fires on 50%. Powered zero. This does not test the ES/NQ claim itself.
Refuted (faithfulness): measures the 08:30 volatility step of a sibling concept, not the clock convention; the null ignores time of day.
Refuted (faithfulness): fixed UTC-5 contradicts the concept's own rules; its excess is summer days where '08:30' is the 09:30 cash open.

Transfer from EU/GU/EURGBP to gold/silver with the XAU/XAG line as the cross. Book: 1h CISD trades opposite a directional dollar (EURUSD proxy), on days the cross has a directional daily closure. Gate: the cross selects gold, against complement days where it selects silver. Diff +0.02R, UNDERPOWERED (MDE 0.23).

Individual-closure variant. Same dollar-filtered 1h CISD book, restricted to trades where exactly one of gold or silver made a daily closure through the prior day in the trade direction. Gate: gold made it, against complement: silver made it. Diff +0.01R, UNDERPOWERED (MDE 0.37).

A list of design exclusions with no directional price claim; its only measurable is a signal count. Several items need data the harness lacks (order flow, DOM, TPO) or are venue choices (futures vs CFD). Each excluded tool is tested under its own id.

Gate on the 15m CISD book. Blocked trades are entries in the direction of a run of 3 or more consecutive daily expansion candles (opposing run/|body| <= 1.0). +0.011R, CI [-0.060, +0.085]. Only 1,164 blocked trades (effective n 192), MDE 0.104, so UNDERPOWERED.
Same gate with a 2-day expansion streak (the 'after two days, wait for a new phase' corollary). +0.016R, CI [-0.026, +0.061]. Powered (MDE 0.062), so NULL.
1h expansion met by an opposite expansion: the rate at which E1's origin is taken within 1,440 M1 bars was 52.9%, against 54.5% for a null at the same distance and horizon. Diff -1.6pp, MDE 6.6pp.
Degraded-sequence filter (claim '-'): aligned 15m CISD continuations where the last three 1h expansions alternate direction. -0.013R vs the rest, powered NULL.
Continuation inside a live 1h expansion: a shallow pullback (<=0.5) into a 15m FVG, then a 15m CISD; stop at the protected swing, target the leg's unswept extreme. +0.020R, MDE 0.104.
Stand-aside after 3 expansion days (claim '-'): aligned 15m CISD continuations after three small-wick trading days in the trade direction. -0.006R, effective n 177.

After a 1h FVG is tagged and respected, does price reach the nearest untaken 2/2 swing (from the last 72 bars) within 3 trading days? It did 74.5% of the time, against 74.4% for a level at the same distance and the same clock time. Powered NULL.

15m proximity reading: two consecutive same-side 3-bar swings within 0.25 ATR14 of each other, the cluster's outer extreme treated as a target. Taken within 300 M1 bars 73.3% of the time vs a 73.7% distance-matched null. Powered NULL.
Refuted (faithfulness): only one horizon is EDGE; 1H and neighbouring horizons NULL; B1 negative.

Trade test on 15m bars. A failure swing is a lower swing high that retraces at least 70% of the prior leg. It is confirmed by a close below the swing bar's low within 8 bars. Stop at the failure-swing extreme, target the lows that produced it (the draw), 24h hold. Result -0.019R vs control: powered NULL (MDE 0.040).
Refuted (faithfulness): the gain is in stops under $0.30 in 2016-18 (microstructure); without them NULL.

Tested the same rule at the daily scale (18:00 NY days, stub days skipped): fade the next day, stop at the day's extreme, target the previous day's opposite extreme, 1380 trading minutes. +0.036R, MDE 0.134, UNDERPOWERED.

Failure branch: a 1h expansion into the prior day's low/high with no opposite expansion within 4 bars, traded as a continuation (stop at the retracement extreme, 2R). +0.129R with a CI excluding 0 in the claimed direction, but MDE 0.110 > 0.10, so the harness labels it UNDERPOWERED.

FVG as an entry array. On the first return to a 1h FVG's near edge within 1,440 M1 bars, enter in the gap's direction, stop beyond the far edge, 2R, 10h hold. Against a matched control: +0.025R, CI [-0.009, +0.059], a powered null (MDE 0.048).
Refuted (both): volatility clustering after displacement - a local-volatility-matched null gives -0.005 NULL.

Union book at the same 1h FVGs, validated-order-block entries vs gap-limit entries. Limit arm: 2R, stop past the gap's far edge. Validated arm: 5m CISD inside the gap, entered on its close, 2R. Validated beat limit by +0.018R, a powered null.

1H gold/silver SMT reversal book (7,796 trades) decided one bar after the SMT. Gate 'genuine' (62% of trades): the sweeping asset closed back inside its level and the held asset has not caught up. Genuine minus fake = +0.005R, CI [-0.066, +0.074], MDE 0.1002, so power just misses.

1-minute step, which is the chart the worked example used. Setup: a 1h FVG tap is the POI, then an M1 close through the intermediate swing, entry at the midpoint of the M1 FVG, stop at the move extreme, target the nearest untaken 1h swing, 8h hold.
The 15-second execution step cannot be tested because the certified data is M1 only. There are no sub-minute bars to find a 15s FVG or swing stop, or to resolve a trade on.

Toolkit tested through its FVG array: first M1 return into a 1h FVG, stop at the far edge, target the most recent 1h swing on the far side (the old high/low), hold 10h. Diff +0.093R, CI [-0.020, +0.226]. The far targets make R highly variable (MDE 0.176), so it is short of power.

Host reading (stand down on the FOMC trading day): gate on the rung-0 15m bare CISD book, non-FOMC days against FOMC days. The sign favours standing down (+0.06R, both halves positive), but the FOMC arm has only 83 days, so it is structurally underpowered.

Guest reading (run the normal process on FOMC days): 15m CISD setups on FOMC trading days against matched random entries come out -0.083R, with the day-block CI excluding 0. Both halves are negative (H1 -0.018, H2 -0.144). This rests on 83 days and p=0.028, so it is fragile under multiplicity.

Never trade after FOMC: 15m CISD decisions from 14:00 NY to the session end on scheduled FOMC days are blocked (125 events on 76 days). Structurally underpowered: effective n is 76 and MDE 0.30. The 'only three releases' preference has no outcome of its own and is not scored.

Within FOMC press-conference weeks (69 dates, each checked against a 14:00 NY volatility spike before testing), 1h CISD trades after the presser day were compared with trades before 14:30 ET on the presser day. The difference was +0.14R, but n_eff was 135 and MDE 0.23, so the result is UNDERPOWERED.
Bare 5m CISD. Setups from 04:00 to 17:00 NY vs setups from 18:00 to 04:00: -0.005R [-0.020, +0.010]. Powered NULL. Discarding pre-04:00 setups gains nothing.

The four-candle window read as a hard window: 5m CISD entries in the direction of the last 1H C2, taken during C3/C4 vs C5/C6. Entries inside the window are not better (powered NULL, point estimate negative).
The C1-C4 numbering convention and the indicator's four-candle display default are labelling definitions that assert nothing about price.
Model 1 on 1m in the 08:30-11:00 NY open: liquidity grab, then BOS close with an FVG, retrace into the FVG, stop at the grab extreme, 2R. A powered zero.
Model 3 vs model 1: requiring the FVG entry to sit in the 0.62-0.79 OTE of the displacement leg. It passes only 11.9% of setups. The MDE of 0.115 exceeds 0.10, so the result is underpowered.

Futures 4H grid, chain pairs 02->06, 06->10 and 10->14 NY. When a candle sweeps one side of the previous 4H candle and closes back inside, trade away from it into the next candle. Stop at the swept extreme, target the prior candle's opposite extreme, 4h hold. Powered NULL (MDE 0.061).

Setup: a small-wick 1h bar closes beyond the prior bar's extreme inside a forming 4H candle (forex grid). Enter at the 50% retrace, stop at the expansion bar's extreme, exit at the 4H close. Result: +0.030R vs control, CI [-0.001, +0.060]. Powered NULL (MDE 0.044).

The C2-unicorn setup pooled over the three stated pairings (15m/1m, 1h/5m, 4h/15m) vs the matched control: -0.019R [-0.059, +0.022]. Powered NULL. Point estimates by pairing: 15m/1m -0.024, 1h/5m -0.065, 4h/15m +0.091 (n=398). Nothing supports it working at every scale.
Refuted (both): forex 4H grid only - futures and UTC grids NULL; fails the ToD-matched control.
The same C2 model on the 1H/5m playbook pairing, one 1h candle hold. Well-powered NULL, +0.005R (MDE 0.027).
4H C3 closure, Reading A: the prior candle took the extreme without a C2 and this candle closes beyond C2's open. Traded C4 at 2R with the stop at the C2/C3 swing, one 4H candle hold. NULL, +0.022R.
4H C3 closure, Reading B: the close must clear C2's extreme, a strict subset of Reading A. Same trade. NULL, +0.019R.

Daily candle 4 trade. Needs a 3-candle swing, with C3 closing beyond C2's extreme and closing strong (close position >= 0.85). Entry at the C4 open, stop at 0.5 of C3's range, 2R, one day held. Only 172 trades in the certified span; -0.107R, UNDERPOWERED.
The same C4 trade on 4H forex-grid candles. Result: -0.040R, MDE 0.120, UNDERPOWERED.
Silver (local OANDA XAG H1) prints a 1H C2 and gold does not. Gold's next hour is traded as C3 on a 5m retracement plus CISD, targeting gold's C2-hour extreme. -0.009R, powered NULL.
Procedure for rolling ES/NQ quarterly contracts by open interest and volume. It makes no claim about price, and XAUUSD spot has no contracts or OI/volume curve.
Ticks, handles and multipliers are units and sizing arithmetic with no market hypothesis. Multipliers cancel in R.

Compares limit fill rates between a futures feed and a spread-quoted forex feed on the same setups. We have one XAUUSD mid M1 series with no bid/ask spread and no futures counterpart, so neither fill rate can be computed.

Compares asset classes: gapping cash equities/ETFs vs continuous futures. Only near-continuous XAUUSD data is available, so gap incidence and profile agreement across instrument classes cannot be measured.

A clock-envelope definition (18:00-17:00 NY, Sun-Fri) with no predictive or trading claim. Its only measurable is a bar-count sanity check, already settled: the daily break resumes at 18:00 NY on 99.8% of 605 halts, and the harness uses that as its day roll. The data is spot gold, not futures.
Vehicle-choice argument (spread, slippage, PDT rule, tax). It needs fills or bid/ask from both venues, and cost cancels in the matched-control differential anyway.

gate_test on the same 1H FVGs (>=0.25 ATR): the 0.5 (CE) entry vs the near-edge entry, same far-edge stop and same fixed target, clustered by gap. Result -0.029R control-adjusted, CI contains 0, MDE 0.18. Only refinement method 1 was tested; methods 2 and 3 have no bounds.

Deep dive: leg extreme is reached before a far-edge close 1-2pp more often, surviving structural controls (+1.05 to +1.80pp); no trade beats a structural-stop control, median stop 0.655pt so every book is net negative.
Refuted (faithfulness): Sunday gaps were matched to quieter weekday reopens; a Sunday-only null cuts the Sunday effect from +16.8 to +3.2pp.

Exception branch: gaps that cross a prior D/W/M extreme should fill LESS often than the null (claim '-'). They filled 35.5% vs a null of 26.2% (+9.3pp), which points against the claim, but the CI contains 0. Only n=110, so underpowered.

Rate test, claim '-'. On gap days (|open - prev close| >= 0.25 ADR20), does price reach a full ADR move from the open against the gap? The null uses random non-gap days within +/-30d at the same distance and direction. 15.7% vs 15.4%. Only 70 gap days on gold, MDE 13.7pp, so UNDERPOWERED.

Six resting limits per 15m structure flip (stop at anchor, target at 0.41), clustered by flip. The gate compared GB levels (0.705/0.7475/0.79) with the concept's own control set (0.5/0.618/0.786). Control-adjusted difference −0.002R, powered NULL (46k fills pooled, 20.9k in the gated arm).
Refuted (both lenses): the effect sits in stale limit fills after the range was already invalidated / target traded; the faithful subset is +0.000R.

Trade: blind limit at 0.7475 of a 15m valid-flip range (the anchor→high range extends until the fill), stop at the anchor, target 0.41 (1.34R), 24h expiry or next opposite flip. Result −0.008R versus the matched control, powered NULL (MDE 0.042).
Head-to-head on 1h C2s where the correlate choices disagree (7,387): reversal SMT vs gold-euro/gold-pound (the instruments he names) against silver-only SMT. No difference, powered NULL (MDE 0.098)
Tested close-based respect after a 4H reversal candle (wick larger than body, forex grid). The test bar is the first 1h bar of the next 4H candle to trade into the wick.
Tested touch-based respect on the same book: the test bar's low stays in the upper half of the wick. +0.034R, MDE 0.109, just above the 0.10 threshold, UNDERPOWERED.
Refuted (both): the -1pp belongs to old untaken levels; unguarded untaken swings fall short of the null by more (-1.96pp).

15m CISD signals fired while a 1D CISD swing is open, split into against the swing (kept as a hedge) and same direction (skipped): +0.010R, NULL. The rule's selection costs nothing per trade, so the exposure reduction comes free. The exposure claim itself is arithmetic.

Tested the premise that a high-resistance extreme (15m pool swept, closing back inside twice) is harder to reach, measured from the next opposite swing: reached 55.6% vs a same-distance null of 56.1% within 360 bars. Powered NULL; the extreme is not harder to reach than its distance implies.

Swing-level sense: a symmetric bracket toward each confirmed 15m swing, gated on a failure swing (lower high / higher low = low resistance) vs a swing that swept the previous one (high resistance). Control-adjusted diff +0.0065R, a powered NULL (MDE 0.025).

Daily-band sense: the first break of PDH or PDL (stop at the day's running extreme, 2R), gated on at least 2 stacked unswept prior daily highs or lows in the path. Diff +0.013R; the gated arm has n=681 and MDE 0.115, so UNDERPOWERED. The corpus's circular 'market-conditions' sense was not tested.

1H close past the HIGH (bearish: LOW) of the opposing series that made the day's running extreme (18:00 NY day) confirms the daily wick; long/short with the stop at the day's extreme, 2R, 10h: +0.014R, a powered NULL.
Same book with the level at the first candle's open (the order-block wording): +0.016R, a powered NULL.

Price engages PDH/PDL. Signal: an hourly close beyond the LOW (bullish: HIGH) of the last opposing candle that engaged it, confirmed 08:30-12:00 NY. Stop at the manipulation extreme, target the -2 SD projection, 10h hold. MDE 0.117 is just short of the 0.10 threshold, so underpowered.

Same as reading a, but the close must be beyond the candle's OPEN (its body). Underpowered (MDE 0.117). Rerun with hold_basis=bars for the trap-7 exposure gap (11%). The first clock run gave +0.053 [-0.029,+0.129]. Weekday/profile step and the 'convincing' qualifier were omitted.

Pure capital structure and sizing with a psychological rationale: deposit only what you can lose, never top up, withdraw the initial, then size up on the rest. It changes neither which trades are taken nor how they exit ('same model at larger size'), so no OHLC outcome can decide it.

Gate on 5m bare CISD. Kept only trades where the 1H and 15m previous-candle narratives (method_spec 2.3) disagree. Trades that followed the 1H narrative did 0.042R worse than trades that followed the 15m one, CI [-0.079, -0.009].

Daily candle governs. Gate on the 15m CISD book: entry at or below the daily open plus 0.25 of the typical range (mirrored for shorts), and the day's range not yet at the 5-day typical range. Result +0.024R [-0.003, +0.050]. Powered, so NULL.
4H candle governs (forex grid). Same gate as reading a, with the 4H candle's open and the mean range of the last 30 4H candles. Result +0.000R [-0.025, +0.025]. Powered, so NULL.
