Rate test: is the Monday high or low traded through by the Friday close? 70.9% against a matched null of 70.8% (same distance, same number of tradable bars, random moments within +/-30 days), rows clustered by week. Monday's extremes are no more of a liquidity target than any level at that distance. Powered NULL.

Trade test of sweep, reject, run from Tuesday to Friday. The first 1h candle through a Monday extreme that closes back inside is the entry; stop at that candle's extreme, target the opposite Monday extreme, hold to Friday 17:00 NY with hold_basis='bars'. Result: -0.318R against the matched control.

Gate test: Monday trades after a Friday C2 reversal against the other Mondays (baseline direction from the §2.3 previous-candle engine). The point estimate leans against the claim (-0.20R). Structurally underpowered: effective n is 89.
Same as reading a, but the Friday C2 must also carry a same-direction 1h CISD. Effective n is 58; UNDERPOWERED.
Baseline: 5m FVG first-return trades (2R, 50 min hold). Gate: the gap overlaps a live same-direction 10m or 15m FVG at the decision. Diff +0.019R, CI [-0.001, +0.038], gate rate 30%. Powered NULL.

15m/5m/1m ladder (M1 stands in for the 15s chart, which is not in the data). Union book of nested-gap entries vs the unrefined 15m-FVG-in-OTE entries at the same legs: +0.028R, CI contains 0, MDE 0.128, underpowered. Both arms enter at the next M1 open, which dilutes the difference.

Trade in the direction of the new day's first-hour colour (both 'flip' days, which were 51% of the sample, and 'confirm' days), skipping hours that were inside bars. Stop 0.5x the prior-day range, exit at 16:00 NY. No better than the matched random control: powered NULL (MDE 0.080).

Gate on the phase-3 15m CISD book (150min hold): decisions in his own-voice NY a.m. window 08:30-12:00 NY vs all other hours. -0.003R, CI [-0.033, +0.027]. The test was powered (MDE 0.043), so this is a NULL: the NY a.m.-only rule adds nothing on gold.

8 a.m. reversal sequence: after a candle-2 closure on the 08:00 NY hourly candle, enter at 09:00 in the reversal direction, stop at the swept extreme, exit at 10:00; controls at the same NY clock. -0.020R, CI contains 0. MDE 0.101 misses the 0.10 threshold by a hair, so UNDERPOWERED.

The day's high or low forms in 09:30-10:00 NY on 10.6% of days, against 4.1% for a random 30-minute window on the same day (lift 2.6x, CI [+5.3pp, +7.9pp], both halves positive). Still UNDERPOWERED under the locked rule: the rate threshold is min(5pp, 25% of the null) = 1.02pp, and the MDE is 1.87pp.
London stayed inside the prior day's range; a 5m CISD off an 08:30-10:00 sweep of the London high/low; target PDH/PDL, flat at 17:00. +0.024R, CI [-0.085,+0.134], MDE 0.157. Underpowered.
Gate on 5m bare CISD. Entries from 09:30 to 11:30 NY (DST-aware) against all other times: +0.012R [-0.012, +0.036]. Powered NULL.
London ran through the midnight open but did not reach PDL/PDH; a 5m CISD in NY 08:30-12:00 off an extreme beyond PDL/PDH; 2R, flat at 17:00. +0.094R, CI [-0.033,+0.210], MDE 0.174. Underpowered.

Stated policy ('nothing changes for me'). Gate on the 1h CISD book: trades on FOMC/NFP release days vs other days, claim '+'; a NULL would be consistent with this reading. -0.019R, CI [-0.12, +0.08], MDE 0.145 with about 204 release days, so it is UNDERPOWERED.

Observed deferral ('waiting for NFP'). Filter that blocks 1h CISD decisions made on a release day before the release (NFP 08:30, FOMC 14:00). +0.008R, CI [-0.13, +0.14]. The blocked arm is only about 192 days (MDE 0.195), so it is UNDERPOWERED.

The red-folder-only reading needs the first red-folder USD event of each week. There is no economic calendar, and only NFP and FOMC dates can be derived. ISM, JOLTS, CPI, PPI, retail sales, GDP, PCE and claims dates cannot, so the week's first driver cannot be identified.

Three-tier reading, rate test: is the weekly high or low printed on a high-impact event day between the release and 17:00 NY? Events are NFP and FOMC presser days. The null uses the same weekday and window in nearby weeks with no NFP or FOMC. Observed 35.4% vs null 24.8%: NFP days 49%, FOMC days 10%.

'Ignore the calendar entirely.' The rule is the same as news-events-ignored reading a, so the test is the same too (same frame and settings, same hypothesis key): release-day vs other-day 1h CISD trades. -0.019R, CI [-0.12, +0.08], UNDERPOWERED.

'I don't trade post FOMC.' Filter that blocks 1h CISD decisions on FOMC days from 14:00 NY to the 18:00 roll. Only 47 blocked events on 39 effective days: +0.07R, CI [-0.19, +0.32], UNDERPOWERED. The '9:30 downgrade' clause is an expectation and was not tested.

The daily next-day decision table was traded on day D+1: continuation (1,132 days) or reversal (868). Entry at the D+1 open, stop at D's extreme, 2R target, one session held in trading time. Result: -0.010R against a matched control, a powered null (MDE 0.064).
After a reversal day (a 2-2 reversal), day D+1 reached D-1's opposite extreme 30.0% of the time, against 30.7% for a null with the same distance and bar count. Powered null (MDE 0.048).

NFP-week day map on the 15m CISD book, NFP weeks only. Allowed = Tue/Wed, release day after 08:30, and any day after the release. Blocked = Mon, the day before the release, and release day before 08:30. Result -0.040R, powered NULL (MDE 0.075).

Friday fade of the NFP sweep of the week-so-far high or low, only in 'internal' weeks. Only 4 of 125 NFP weeks met the declared internal test and 3 of those produced a trade, so n=3 < 30 and the harness verdict is UNTESTABLE. The trade itself is fully operationalised.

9:30 drive trade: enter at the 09:30 open toward the nearer untaken previous-day high or low. Stop at the far-side 08:30-09:30 pre-open extreme (the kill condition), target that extreme, time exit 12:00; clock-fixed controls. +0.080R, CI [-0.026, +0.199].

Rauf reading on the 1h CISD book: trade only when the last month and the last week both closed beyond the prior period's high or low (27% of events pass). -0.021R [-0.083, +0.038]. The month-clustered CI leaves an effective n of 59, so it is UNDERPOWERED.

Daily-draw reading (Jokerszn/Nick close-through test) on the 1h CISD book: trade only after the prior day closed beyond the day-before's high or low. Allowed trades did worse than those taken on an inside-close day: -0.064R [-0.113, -0.011], NEGATIVE.
Refuted (both): depends on the locked control draw: six other seeds give +0.017 to +0.032 (mean +0.025) against +0.031 reported, at the edge of significance.
Refuted (faithfulness): its distinguishing small-wick test does nothing (-0.012R); knife-edge wick cut.
Plain 'never trade Monday' (18:00-NY session date) on the 15m CISD book. Tue-Fri vs Monday: -0.010R, powered NULL (MDE 0.045).
AM Trades form: Monday blocked, and Tuesday allowed only if Monday traded through the prior week's high or low. Result: powered NULL (MDE 0.037).

Daily 09:30 fade: fade the 09:30-09:45 leg, stop at the leg's extreme, 2R, exit 16:00. No-news days (n=1,685) vs news days (n=972): +0.020R [-0.10, +0.14]. News days are derived NFP Fridays plus an 08:30 5m range at least 3x its 24h median; there is no calendar data. MDE 0.17, so UNDERPOWERED.

15m STRAT 2-2 trades with continuity. At each 15m close while a trade is alive (up to 16 bars), score 'keep holding' (original stop, no target, 1h), clustered by trade. Holding after a close with no opposing 2 (69k rows) vs holding after the opposing-2 close (16k rows): -0.018R [-0.050, +0.012]. Powered NULL;
Gate on the 15m rung-0 CISD book (both directions): shorts closing below the previous-day low (or longs above the previous-day high) vs the rest, claim '-'. NULL: chasing beyond PDH/PDL is not worse.
Verifiers upheld (-0.038R, all 4 blocks negative) but BH q=0.16 - a candidate only: shorting 15m CISDs at the running day low underperforms.

Untestable: this is pure sizing arithmetic. Position size changes dollars, never a trade's R outcome, and the concept claims no market effect in either direction to test. The 34% break-even at 2R is the identity 1/(1+2).

Base book: 1h CISD with T1 = nearest unbroken 1h swing at least 0.25R away. At the first adverse 15m close through the latest 15m swing before T1 or the stop, holding the original stop/T1 bracket for the rest of the 10h hold vs a matched random control: -0.028R [-0.073, +0.021].

Longs only in the 1h CISD book. Blocked when the 2R target sits above the running ATH, taken as the larger of the pre-sample 1921.17 and the in-data maximum (301 blocked). +0.033R [-0.102, +0.159]. Only 187 effective days, so UNDERPOWERED.
The rule picks between NQ and ES futures by relative volatility and weekly relative weakness. The dataset is single-instrument XAUUSD, so there is no second series to choose between.

Rate test on 30m candles, bias = prior-day candle direction, opposing-run and expansion cuts from threshold_fits at 1.0. Two branches pooled: an 8:30 opposing run predicts a 9:30 expansion; if 8:30 fails and 9:30 runs, it predicts a 10:00 expansion.

Daily previous-candle bias; after 08:30 NY, a sweep of the 00:00-08:30 range extreme on the bias side (so below the midnight open for longs); 5m CISD entry, stop at the swept extreme, target the far side of that range, exit 16:00. +0.048R, MDE 0.137, UNDERPOWERED.

Order-type mechanics with no claim to test: a limit entry with an OCO stop and target. The harness already resolves every trade as an OCO bracket, so there is nothing to compare it against. Stop-leg slippage needs fill or tick data, and no rule says where the limit goes.

Reading (a), the mirrored curve. A respected left-side 4H order block before a confirmed 4H swing is broken by a close on the return leg. The first 1H retrace into the band is traded as the re-polarised block: stop beyond the zone, 2R, 48h hold. Result: +0.002R vs control, CI [-0.076, +0.083], MDE 0.114.

Reading (b), old gaps. Book: 3,868 4H FVG retests, traded as a reaction from the approach side (stop at the far edge, 2R, 48h). Old retests (traded into, 2 or more bars of accumulation, departed, then retouched within 60 days; 49% of the book) are compared with fresh first touches.

After a 15m CISD reversal: opposite FVGs from the prior leg are closed through, then retested as support/resistance. Stop at the protected swing, 2R (stop and target borrowed from the method spec because the concept gives neither). NULL.
Refuted (both): rests on the locked-seed control draw; ToD-matched control halves it to NULL.

Rate test: the day's first 15m CISD between 02:00 and 12:00 NY. Claim tested: its protected swing is the daily wick and is not traded through before the 17:00 NY halt. It held 24.4% of the time vs 25.5% for a null at matched distance, time of day and bar count: -0.011 [-0.029, +0.008]. Powered NULL (MDE 0.026).

5m swing-level breaks. Entering on the first M1 close through the level (n=102k) vs waiting for the 5m close (n=98k), same 5m swing stop, 2R, 50-minute hold: +0.006R, CI [-0.004, +0.016]. Powered NULL (MDE 0.014).

Framework one: the 4H candle opens between the 1.0 and 1.5 deviation, and the claim is continuation to -2. Hit 66.7% vs 68.5% for a same-moment mirror level at the same distance in the opposite direction; that null was fixed before the run.

Framework two: the candle opens between the 2.0 and 2.5 deviation, and the claim is a retracement to the previous candle's 50% level. Hit 61.7% vs 64.6% for the same-moment mirror level. The point estimate is negative and the test is underpowered (MDE 0.078).
Tested a daily PO3 anchored at the NY midnight open, with 15m bars. The trigger is the first close back through the open after a manipulation that also closes through the pre-extreme swing.
Ash's reading. Bare 5m CISD taken within 60 minutes of 02:00 or 09:30 NY vs all other times: -0.002R [-0.027, +0.023]. Powered NULL.
$niper and AM Trades' reading. Bare 5m CISD taken 09:30-12:00 NY vs all other times: +0.008R [-0.013, +0.029]. Powered NULL.
Qualification rule: 15m CISD whose opposing-series candles all have a wick on the extreme side, vs series containing a wickless candle (1,872 in the complement). +0.044R, powered NULL.

Rolling invalidation: inside a live 1h expansion, enter with the trend at each qualifying opposing 1h candle close. Stop beyond the series extreme, target the leg extreme. +0.039R; effective n 2,274 with heavy dependence and 12.7% control overlap, MDE 0.181.
Refuted (faithfulness): a knife-edge 0.30 cut - every neighbouring cut and the futures 4H grid are NULL.

Trade test. Setup: with the previous-candle daily bias, a counter-bias 5m opposing run from the 00:00, 08:30 or 09:30 NY open, then a CISD close back through it. Enter on that close, stop at the run's extreme, 2R, exit at 16:00 NY (hold measured in bars, clustered by date).

Gate test of the Judas-swing price anchor on reading a's 08:30/09:30 trades. Gate = the run's extreme lies beyond both the midnight open and the 08:30 open. Gated n=958 vs 710: +0.048R [-0.092, +0.185]. MDE 0.198, so UNDERPOWERED.
Bare 0.705 OTE limit on 15m close-through displacement legs (stop at the leg anchor, target the leg extreme, 5h hold) vs matched random entry: +0.001R, a powered null.
Gate on the OTE book: does a same-direction 15m FVG overlapping the 0.62-0.79 band help? -0.026R, CI contains 0. MDE 0.12 is above the 0.10 threshold, so underpowered.
Expiry-selection rule against theta decay. It needs option premia or implied vol, which the campaign lacks, and the corpus gives no method for estimating time-to-target.
Frame the setup on NQ and execute an at-the-money QQQ option. Testing it needs option chain prices and an ETF; the campaign has only gold M1 OHLC.

1h order block, structural validation. A 2/2 extreme raids the last confirmed swing. The opposing-close run into it is validated by a close through the run's far extreme (low of the up-close run, high of the down-close run) within 3 bars. Retest the block's opening price within 24h, stop at the extreme, 2R, 10h.
Refuted (implementation lens): disappears under the time-of-day-matched control (trap 9).

Gate test on first returns to the opening price of 1h CISD order blocks (limit-touch entry, protected-swing stop, 2R, 10h). Gate = high-probability block candle, meaning opposing_run/body <= 1.0 (threshold_fits grade A). High-probability blocks (n=3788) vs low-probability (1790): +0.080R [+0.0003, +0.154].

On 15m swing breaks, compared a limit return to the breaking candle (AP's BOS order block) with a return to the last opposing candle of the same break. Entry at the near body edge, stop at the far wick, 2R, 150min, clustered by break. Powered NULL, leaning against the claim (the CI upper bound is +0.0008).

Baseline: retest entries at the CISD-born block level of 5m blocks with a series of >= 2 candles (stop at the protected swing, 2R, 50 min). Gate: the series collapses into one 15m candle that closed in the series' direction. NULL, powered.

Baseline is the rung-3 book (1h CISD, 2R, 10h). Gate is rung 2: an opposing FVG closed fully through between the extreme and the CISD, which fired on 26.5% of events. With vs without the inversion: -0.008R [-0.063, +0.046]. Powered null.

The rule's only operative step is footprint/DOM confirmation (tape speed, buy/sell aggression) at the ICT level. The data is M1 OHLC spot XAU_USD with no volume, no trade-side classification and no order book. The guest also gives no threshold for any of it.

Tight-stop profile on 5m CISD entries, which stand in for the order-flow entry: stop 0.0625% of price (2.5 ES points), target 3.2R, 50-minute hold. avg_R -0.050 against a matched random entry: -0.013R [-0.024, -0.003], NEGATIVE. Ties are negligible.

Tested whether the block extreme gets taken later in the day when the Asia low/high coincides with the PDL/PDH (within 0.10 daily ATR) and the Asia range is choppy (at most 0.5 ATR). It was hit 70.9% of the time against a matched null of 72.4%. Powered NULL.

Tested option A, the 50% mark of an oversized gap (5m FVGs at least 1 ATR(20)), against the near-edge entry he warns against, on the same gaps. Stop at the far edge, 2R target, 50min hold, clustered by gap. Control-adjusted +0.035R, CI contains 0, powered (MDE 0.059), so NULL.

Reading A (TTrades): half the position exits at 2R and half runs to the prior day's high or low, compared with one full exit at that level. Entries: 1h CISD where that level is at least 2R away. The difference was +0.005R, CI [-0.076, +0.087], underpowered. The trailed runner cannot be modelled;
Reading B (the guest): no intraday partials, one full exit at the draw, claim '+'. This is the same comparison as reading a with the opposite claim: -0.005R, CI [-0.094, +0.078], underpowered.

Tested as a target rule on the phase-3 locked 1h CISD entry book: target = near edge of the nearest unmitigated opposite 1h FVG (ladder step 1), stop at the protected swing, 10h hold. Against a control with matched stop and target distances: +0.017R, CI contains 0, powered, so NULL. Unfilled FVGs do not act as magnets.

Daily FVGs: first retest within 10 bars, traded with the array (stop at its far side, 2R). Gate: the retest bar did not close beyond the mean threshold. The gate passes 91% of the time, so the complement is only 33 trades. Result -0.29R, CI [-0.87, +0.27].
Same book on 1H FVGs. Retests that held the mean threshold vs retests that closed beyond it: +0.012R, CI [-0.108, +0.137]. The halves disagree. MDE 0.176 because the complement is only 638 trades.

Rule tested: after 3 or more consecutive daily expansion closures, a continuation trade is worse (claim '-'). Run as a gate on the daily continuation book (next-session open, stop at the day's EQ (midpoint of the range), target the day's extreme). Only 124 gated trades against 1,026 in the complement;

Rule tested: a daily expansion met by an opposite daily expansion is a reversal; trade away from the two-day wick with a 2R target and a 5-session hold. 127 trades, +0.03R versus the matched control; n < 200, so the verdict cannot be NULL.

Reversal branch on 15m: an expansion followed within 24 bars by an opposite expansion, traded that way (stop at E1's extreme, target E1's origin). +0.017R vs control, CI includes 0, MDE 0.124. Half the events were dropped because the origin was already taken at entry.
Bias alignment: 15m rung-0 CISD traded with vs against the direction of the latest 1h expansion. +0.025R, powered NULL.

Gate test on 1h STRAT runs of 2 or more same-direction 2s that reverse with an opposite 2. Stop at the run extreme, target the base of the stack, 24h hold. The gate is a run of 5 or more (8% of 5,297 events, 421 gated). Result +0.097R, CI [-0.13, +0.33]: UNDERPOWERED (MDE 0.325). Locked at 1h, so no re-run on 15m.
Refuted (faithfulness): every entry is 10:00 NY and the ToD-matched control removes it; tests a superset of the concept.

Forex 4H grid (the grid the method spec locks for gold). A 05:00 C2 reversal against 01:00, then trade the 09:00 candle with the same stop, 2R target and 4h hold. +0.039R with a CI that includes 0. Powered NULL, just barely (MDE 0.096).
Refuted (faithfulness): the CISD-level POI branch passes almost automatically (29% of events pass with no POI).

5m CISD book (50min hold), limited to events whose extreme bar traded through a prior 1D/4h/1h/1W/1M high or low. Gate: in-band POIs only (1D/4h/1h) vs events that tagged a weekly or monthly level. +0.018R, CI [-0.04, +0.07].

Deep dive: the gate split survives structural controls (+0.10 to +0.12R) but is a negative filter - CISDs off a non-extreme HL/LH lose ~0.08R; gated book gross +0.042R nets -0.009R at 0.30pt. BH q=0.049, Holm fails.

Same 1h CISD baseline. Gate is the loose closed list: any FVG tagged or any prior swing taken in the range, with no fallback and no both-required clause. Pass rate 64.4%. Gated vs complement: -0.048R [-0.106, +0.004]. Powered null that leans against the claim.

Pure sizing arithmetic (risk = drawdown/N). Rescaling R cannot change a book's control-adjusted expectancy, and surviving N losses holds by construction. It needs a strategy's loss-streak distribution and a firm's rules, not a claim about gold.

Fixed-dollar risk with size solved from the stop is a sizing procedure. The harness already scores every book in constant-R terms, so there is no alternative arm, and contract/micro rounding is a futures spec absent from spot data.

4H C2 on the forex grid. Entry at the C3 open, stop on the latest 15m CISD protected swing inside C2, which had to sit beyond C2's EQ (xMFd_kfmIqI selection test). 2R target, 240 trading-minute hold (hold_basis bars). Not better than a matched random entry (powered, MDE 0.053).

'Invalidation very close to the open' variant: daily C2, 1H protected swing within 0.25 of the C2 range from the close, held one session. Only 32 events in 10.5 years, because the swing is usually the day's extreme, far from the close. Cannot be decided.

Trade test of pre-09:30 NY entries (07:00-09:30): 15m CISD with a protected-swing stop, the last closed 1D, 4H and 1H candles all in the trade direction, target PDH/PDL at least 2R away, exit by 16:00. Control held to the same NY hours (+/-30 min). Result -0.19R [-0.46, +0.09] on 181 trades, MDE 0.39. UNDERPOWERED.
Same setup, decided 07:00-12:00 NY. Gate compares pre-open entries (before 09:30) with post-open entries (09:30-12:00). Result -0.35R [-0.88, +0.14], 181 pre-open against 69 post-open. UNDERPOWERED.

Session AMD: a London excursion beyond one side of the Asia range, then a 15m CISD closing back inside the range. Target the opposite Asia extreme; stop at the manipulation extreme. 764 trades, -0.017R [-0.10,+0.07]. MDE 0.124, underpowered.

Candle-level AMD on the 18:00 daily open: manipulation beyond the open, then a 15m CISD from the day's extreme closing back through the open. Target the -2SD projection of the manipulation leg. +0.016R [-0.035,+0.070]. Powered null.

NFP only, with dates from the BLS reference-week rule (95% show an 08:30 volatility spike). Blocked: the pre-NFP days of the week, NFP day before 08:30, and any hold that spans the release. Allowed minus blocked is -0.065R [-0.141, +0.013]. MDE 0.110, so UNDERPOWERED; the point estimate runs against the claim.

Tested the orthodox earlier recording: longs only below the NY midnight open and shorts only above it, as a gate on the 15m CISD-at-POI book (2R, 150 min, events 00:00-17:00 NY). -0.031R, powered NULL.

Tested the inverted later canon: longs only while price is above the previous trading day's EQ and shorts only below it, on the same 15m CISD book. It is applied to all events because there is no mechanical expansion-phase classifier. +0.009R, powered NULL.

Range = latest confirmed 4H (forex grid) swing high and low, re-anchored to the running extreme. On the 15m CISD book, entries whose price sits in the correct half (longs below EQ, shorts above) show no difference. Powered, MDE 0.041.
Structure-point variant: the CISD's protected swing (the higher low or lower high) sits in the discount (longs) or premium (shorts) of the 4H range. No difference. Powered, MDE 0.043.

Still-untaken 2- and 3-day-old daily highs/lows, reached during the next session: 19.3% vs a null of 19.9% at the same distance, measured from other session opens. Powered NULL. The 1-day-old level is covered by previous-period-high-low.

Draw reading: PDH/PDL reached during the next session 46.8% of the time, against 48.6% for a level at the same distance from the session open on another day within +/-30 days. The CI excludes 0 against the claim. PDH/PDL are slightly LESS likely to be reached than an arbitrary equidistant level.

Reversal-case reading: day D-1 swept one side of D-2 and closed back inside, and D-2's opposite extreme is the target on day D. It was reached 29.2% of the time vs a null of 31.3%. Powered NULL (MDE 0.046 <= 0.05).

A plan for running many prop accounts (trailing drawdown, payout schedules, account count). Nothing to test in XAU OHLC: the aggressive phase has no entry, stop or size, and the '100 ticks / close once profitable enough' exit has no entry model and no defined threshold.

A prop-firm size ladder (a ~$2,000 cushion, then about 20 micros, then 1-5 ES). This is sizing arithmetic tied to a firm's drawdown rules and the trader's own confidence. There is no setup, R does not change with size, and testing it needs prop-account equity records.
Prop-account sizing and economics (percent of drawdown tiers, drawdown-to-target ratio, fees). This is arithmetic plus firm terms, none of which is in XAUUSD OHLC, and no gold test can decide it.

UNTESTABLE. Defines how prop firms compute drawdown (static, EOD-trailing, unrealised-trailing, DLL + MLL). These are contract definitions with no claim about XAUUSD price. Breach probability depends on a strategy's P&L path under firm terms, not on OHLC.
Refuted (both): a placebo with the same limit-fill mechanics and no block gives +0.025; ToD control NULL.
Refuted (both): the limit-fill emulation (dropping fills that close through the stop) produces the edge, not the block.
1h protected swing: a strict POI (a prior swing swept or an FVG reached, no fallback), then a close through the series' OPEN within 3 bars. Stop on the swing, 2R. -0.009R, powered NULL.
Same as reading a, but the close must go through the series' far EXTREME. -0.002R, powered NULL.

The nearer previous-month extreme was reached before the far one 42.0% of the time, against 49.4% for a null with the same two distances and horizon. That is the opposite of the claim. Clustered by month, effective n=114. Re-run once after a bug in my null (details in the note).

Gold 1H C2 book (entry at the C2 close, stop at the C2 extreme, 2R, 10h), gated on a candle-two PSP with silver (the C2 hour closes opposite colours in gold and silver): no difference from C2s without a PSP. Powered, MDE 0.073.
Same gold 1H C2 book, gated on a candle-one PSP (gold and silver close opposite colours on C1): no difference. Powered, MDE 0.075.

Rate test over sessions in quarter-end closing weeks. Share of small-range days (range below the median of the prior 20 sessions): 45.9% against a null of 51.0% from other weeks within +/-30 days. The difference points against the dampener claim, and n=196 is too few to decide.

Same small-range-day test on every month-end closing week: 48.2% against a null of 51.7%, diff -0.035 [-0.074, +0.004]. Leans against the claim. MDE 0.056 is above the 0.05 threshold, so UNDERPOWERED.

Consolidation = the day after an inside day (range = mother candle). Gate: 15m CISD entries in the outer 25% of the range, pointing back inward, vs all other in-range entries (523 vs 3,537). -0.157R [-0.270,-0.041]. Both halves are negative; ties are negligible.
Gate on the 15m CISD book: block entries whose decision close sits at 0.40-0.60 of the prior day's range. Allowed minus blocked is -0.011R [-0.046, +0.025], NULL and powered (MDE 0.051).

Gate test on the guest's own model: 1h leg of at least 1 ATR, M1 touch of the 50% retracement, stop at the leg origin, target at the leg extreme, 10h hold. Expansive regime (48-bar 1h efficiency ratio >= 0.20, gated n=3,051) vs range-bound (n=6,393): +0.046R [-0.020, +0.108]. Powered NULL (MDE 0.091).

Transfer from ES/NQ to XAU/XAG, H1 only. Signal: the ratio line's close breaks its 20-bar high (or low), then closes back inside on the next bar. The benchmark 4H/15m model at a fixed 2R with no management. Entries: 15m CISD in the direction of the 4H previous-candle bias (forex grid). It did not beat matched random entries (+0.006R, CI [-0.016, +0.029]): a powered null. Raw win rate was 42%, against the claimed 63% (recorded in notes only; not a verdict input).
Post-creation rebalance: 1h FVG fully filled (M1 touch of the far edge within 5D), then trade the reversal in the gap's direction, stop 1 gap height beyond, 2R, 10h hold. +0.026R, powered NULL.

Pre-creation daily rebalance: C3 opens beyond C1's extreme but inside C2's range. Race: does C1's extreme get touched before C2's extreme? 36.9% vs geometry null 36.2%, powered NULL. The 'majority of candles' claim is not borne out either (37% raw).

Gold 1h CISD book gated on gold being the right asset against silver by tool 3 (closure): the confirming candle's body in own-ATR units beats silver's for a long, trails it for a short. Gate fires on 58%. Powered zero.
Same book, gated by tool 2 (separation): gold travelled further than silver from the shared reversal bar, in own-ATR units, in the trade direction. Gate fires on 62%. Powered, CI contains 0.

Gold 1H rung-0 CISD book, gated on separation strength against silver: longs kept when gold's close sits closer to its PDH (scaled by its own prior-day range) than silver's does, shorts when gold sits closer to its PDL. Slightly positive but the CI contains 0. Powered, MDE 0.076.
Same book, gated on the swing-point test: gold's reach beyond the shared PDH (or PDL) today, scaled by its own range, is larger than silver's. NULL, powered.

Target reading. Untaken 1h equal-high/low pools (consecutive 2/2 swings within a declared tolerance of 0.10xATR14) were reached within 3 trading days 84.7% of the time, against 82.7% for a level at the same distance and the same NY clock time. Powered, CI contains 0.

'Do not trade away from equal highs' reading, run as a gate on the phase-3 1h CISD book. Reversals whose extreme is equal to the previous same-side swing (8% of the book) came in -0.048R vs the rest, in the claimed direction but not significant. MDE 0.156 is above 0.10, so the test is underpowered.

London run with a 15m CISD at the London extreme that reached PDH/PDL. Does that extreme hold for the rest of the day more often than a clock-matched null? 37.8% vs 36.7%; n=209 is below the power floor.

Fake CISD: a London CISD extreme that did NOT reach PDH/PDL. Is it re-run the same day more often than a clock-matched null? 63.5% vs 65.6%, sign against the claim; n=400 is underpowered (MDE 0.072 vs 0.05).

Gate on the 1h CISD book: the reversal extreme took PDH/PDL. The previous-week extremes are nested inside that, and it is the attested default relevant-level set. The gate fired on 23% of the book; gated minus complement was +0.025R [-0.032, +0.080]. Powered NULL.

Gate on the 1h CISD book: the reversal extreme took an untaken 1h swing formed inside the three-daily-candle window, the relevant-swing lookback. The gate fired on 21% of the book; result +0.031R [-0.028, +0.089]. Powered NULL.

1h CISD reversals that swept an untaken 1h swing from the last 20 trading days, gated on at least one swept swing lying inside the 3-daily-candle window. Gate fires on 97.9%, so the complement has an effective n of 64.

1h CISD reversals off an internal extreme that has an untaken outer same-side swing in the 3-day window. Gate: separation from that outer swing >= 0.5 ADR (declared). Gate fires on only 8.6% (median separation 0.11 ADR), so the gated arm is too small: MDE 0.17.

Book that fades the first touch of every 1h 3-candle swing inside its 3-day window (stop 0.5 ATR1h beyond, 2R, 10h), gated on the swing being relevant: no untaken outer same-side swing within 0.5 ADR. Gate fires on 21% of 23,840 touches. Powered zero.
SLOW reading: a shallow retracement that takes at least as long as the 1h expansion leg, then a 15m CISD continuation (stop L, target H). -0.078R, on the wrong side of the claim, MDE 0.118.
QUICK reading: a shallow retracement shorter than the expansion leg, then a 15m CISD continuation. +0.019R, powered NULL (MDE 0.079).

Path test. Baseline: 1,030 one-sided daily C2s, entered at the next open, stop at the C2 extreme, target at the C2's opposite extreme, held one trading day. Gate: the candle made its low before its high (open-low-high-close), checked on M1. -0.056R, CI [-0.195, +0.086]; effective n 378, so it is badly underpowered.
Shape test on the same daily C2 book. Gate: opposing run larger than the body (large wick, small body). +0.041R, CI [-0.061, +0.150], MDE 0.15. The daily sample is too small to decide.

Day took PDL/PDH; a 1h CISD off the day's extreme with price still beyond the 18:00 open; target the daily open, flat at 17:00. +0.002R, CI [-0.057,+0.060], MDE 0.083. Powered null: the open is no magnet.
Same entries, target = the day's opposing extreme so far (the variant). +0.006R, CI [-0.064,+0.072], MDE 0.097. Powered null.

Tested the primary reading: a 1h extreme that takes PDH/PDL or PWH/PWL, followed within 3 candles by a CISD close through the series open. Traded away from the extreme, stop at the extreme, 2R, 10h exit. +0.023R vs the matched control, powered NULL.

Tested the variant definition: the reading-a book plus an SMT, meaning XAG_USD had not taken its own counterpart of the PD/PW level gold took by the closing candle. n=456, +0.030R, MDE 0.142, UNDERPOWERED.

Baseline: 5m structure breaks with displacement (threshold_fits N=4, r=1.5, d=0.65), traded in the reversal direction. Gate: the 15m structure is still intact in the original trend; claim '-' (those should be mere pullbacks). NULL, powered: the 15m hierarchy makes no difference. Re-run once after a bug fix;
Reading a, stop after the second loss of the day ($niper / Trader T): trades before the second daily loss vs trades after it. Powered NULL, +0.012R [-0.019, +0.042].
Reading b, at most 1 trade a day and 2 a week (the variant definition): the gated arm has only 1,101 trades. MDE 0.107 is above the 0.10 threshold, so UNDERPOWERED, +0.038R [-0.037, +0.113].

Tested 2R as a floor. The book was 1h CISD entries targeting the prior day's high or low; the gate kept setups where that target was at least 2R away (33% of 6,065). Floor-passing setups did no better than the rest (-0.040R, CI [-0.114, +0.030]). The test was just short of power (MDE 0.1025).

Compared a fixed 2R target with a fixed 1R target on the same 1h CISD entries. Each arm was adjusted by its own matched control. The difference was +0.002R, CI [-0.031, +0.034]: a powered null (MDE 0.046). The script was run twice because the first write was refused on a params_source prefix;

Target fixed first at the untaken prior-day high/low. The 15m CISD is traded when its R >= 2. Otherwise the book takes the earliest 5m or 1m CISD that gives R >= 2 to the same target, inside 150 minutes and before the target or the 15m stop is touched. Trades by timeframe: 15m 17,129; 1m 4,824; 5m 334.

Gate test on the 15m first-flip plus second-break book, with identical stop and 2R trades, clustered by flip. The gate is the second continuation break. Result -0.022R vs the first flip: powered NULL (MDE 0.063). The HTF key-area split the speaker leaves open was not tested.

5m pattern: a 3h box (range at most 4x the mean bar range), a close beyond it, a 30-min second box at most half the first's range, then a breakout close. Stop at the second box, 2R. Only 103 events under the knobs declared before the run; diff -0.096R, CI [-0.38, +0.19].

Tested the stand-aside rule as a gate with claim '-'. Baseline: 15m bare CISD trades in NY 08:30-12:00. Gate: S&D day, meaning London takes both Asia extremes and closes back inside the Asia range (about 5% of days). Result: diff -0.004R, MDE 0.19, effective n 128.

Outside-in deviation trade on S&D days: a 15m bar in NY AM takes London's high or low and closes back inside. Target is London EQ, stop is the deviation extreme, hold 150 min. Too few trades to decide.

Rate test, because the concept gives no stop. Event: the first 15m wick outside the Asia range (20:00-00:00 NY) that closes back inside with no earlier displacement close. Outcome: the Asia EQ is reached by 12:00 NY: 76.3% vs a matched null of 76.3%. Powered NULL.
Seek-and-destroy day (both Asia extremes taken): fade every 15m deviation that closes back inside the Asia range, stop at the deviation extreme, target rung 1 (the range EQ). Powered and NULL.

Same deviations as reading a, targeting rung 3 (the opposite Asia boundary). CI contains 0 and MDE is 0.113 against the 0.10 threshold, so underpowered. Rung 2 (OTE) was not tested because the leg is unspecified.

Kill-zone chain (prior NY AM, Asia, London, NY AM); manipulation = sweep of the prior window closing back inside. 15m CISD events in the predicted expansion session vs other sessions, with the control matched to NY clock time (ctrl_tod_tol_min=30). Result -0.026R, powered NULL (MDE 0.077).

Forex Asia (20-00 NY) and London (02-05 NY) highs and lows, reached before 12:00 NY: 71.2% vs a null of 71.6% at the same distance and the same NY minute (+/-30 min, +/-30 days). Asia levels hit 73.1%, London 69.3%. Powered NULL. The two displacement rules need an undefined displacement measure and were not tested.
Pure-clock rate test, paired by day. Step-up = the 15-minute M1 range after T is larger than the 15 minutes before. The claim for forex-class gold is that 08:30 is the time level and 09:30 is not.
Tests the 08:30 step-up on NFP days (dates from the BLS rule; the only news calendar that can be derived) against 08:30 on random non-NFP weekdays within +/-30 days.
5m (H1/M5) CISD book inside the three sessions. Gated = London or NY a.m., where the map permits M5, vs Asia, where it does not. Powered NULL, -0.010R.
3m (30m/3m) CISD book. Gated = NY a.m., where the map permits M3, vs Asia and London. Powered NULL, +0.001R.

7h candles anchored at 18:00, so London is 01:00-08:00. After a London C2 reversal, New York (08:00-15:00) held the London candle's 50% level (or 50% of its wick when the wick is large) with no M1 close through it on 28.7% of days. The null, same distance at a similar NY time, held on 26.9%.

Baseline: 4,559 continuation trades. Each is the first 5m CISD after a pullback inside a confirmed 1h impulse leg (a close through a swing), stop at the pullback extreme, 2R. Gate: pullback depth below 0.618 of the leg (74% shallow, median depth 0.43). +0.057R, CI [-0.017, +0.129], MDE 0.104, effective n 1,016.

Mechanical re-run of the silver-bullet AM model on gold. A sweep of the 09:00 NY hourly range during 10:00-11:00 NY, then a 1m CISD in the other direction. Stop at the swept extreme, target the far side of the range, 5h hold. Median planned RR was 3.8.

Raid of the 09:00 NY hour's high or low between 10 and 11, a 1m CISD entry, stop at the sweep extreme, target the other side of the 09:00 candle, 120-minute hold, control matched on time of day. -0.011R, MDE 0.131 > 0.10, so UNDERPOWERED.

Structural Silver Bullet: a 1h close through a breaker after a sweep. Stop at the reversal extreme, target the 5-day original consolidation, 48h hold. Gate: the Silver Bullet forms below 50% of the dealing range.
The conflicting time-window definition, applied as a gate on the same structural breaker book: the breaker bar is the 10:00-11:00 NY hour. Result -0.007R, n=167 gated, so UNDERPOWERED.

Gate on the 5m bare CISD book: decision inside 10:00-11:00 NY, so every fill lands inside the window (entry by 10:55). +0.004R against the rest of the day. Powered NULL. The draw-on-liquidity precondition is not modelled; the concept only states the window.

C3 traded off the single C2 CISD alone: a 4h forex-grid C2 with a same-direction 15m CISD inside it, entered at the C2 close with the stop at the C2 extreme, 2R, held to the C3 close. Against matched random entries: +0.014R [-0.015, +0.044]. Powered null (MDE 0.042).

Reading a, size down after an extended winning run (declared as 3 winners in a row), claim '-'. Trades after the run come out slightly better, not worse, and the CI contains 0: powered NULL, +0.037R [-0.026, +0.098]. The 'would tilt you' trigger is subjective and was not tested.

Reading b, size down when volatility has risen: mean 15m true range over the last day at or above 1.5x its 20-day mean (declared), claim '-'. Powered NULL, -0.009R [-0.079, +0.058], MDE 0.098. This probe is the one that caught both _book.py bugs.

Every directional 4H candle, traded as a continuation into the next 4H candle: stop at the candle's opposite extreme, time exit only. The gate is a small wick (opposing run / body <= 1.0). Result: +0.016R, a powered null (MDE 0.070).
Same 4H continuation book with the range form of the small-wick gate (opposing run / range <= 0.30). Result: +0.025R, a powered null (MDE 0.061).

Book: 4H forex-grid candles that swept the prior 4H candle and closed back inside. Gate: small opposing wick (opposing run / body at most 1.0) against large wick, with a 2R stop at the candle extreme. Diff +0.028R, CI contains 0, MDE 0.135: UNDERPOWERED.

Components reading, 15m. Required: the extreme swept the prior-day low/high, a CISD close, an inversion (close through the last opposing FVG) and a 1/1 short-term low within 8 bars. Stop at the extreme, 2R, 150 min. Result: -0.024R, CI [-0.060, +0.015], powered NULL.

Finessee_Fx's 'always at a HTF PD array' claim, as a gate on the bare 15m CISD book. Pass = the extreme sits inside an unmitigated same-side daily FVG or daily order block no more than 60 days old. Gated 27.8% of the book. Result: -0.007R, CI [-0.037, +0.024], powered NULL.

1H breaker: low, high, lower low, then a body close above the up-close run into the high. Entry on the return into the block when fair value coincides (FVG overlap or the leg's 50% inside the block). Stop at the lower low, 2R, 10h. Result: +0.030R, CI [-0.011, +0.071], powered NULL.

Reading A (SMT confirms an existing model). Baseline: the phase-3 1h CISD book (protected-swing stop, 2R, 10h). Gate: a same-direction hourly gold/XAG SMT printed in the 3h up to the CISD close. The gate fires on 17% of trades; control-adjusted diff +0.013R, CI [-0.065, +0.092].

Reading B (trade the SMT directly). Takes the SMTs where silver swept and gold held, enters gold with the stop at gold's held low/high, 2R target, 10h. Diff vs the matched control is -0.013R, CI [-0.058, +0.034]. Powered NULL (MDE 0.066).

4H gold/silver SMT, then the lagging (held) asset trades through its level within 20 bars, and gold is traded as a reversal at that close (stop at the extreme, 2R, 40h hold). Result: -0.040R vs matched control, CI [-0.116, +0.039], MDE 0.111 above the 0.10 threshold. Only the two-asset arrangement could be tested;

Bare hourly gold/XAG SMT at a shared 2/2 swing (lows bullish, highs bearish), traded in gold with a symmetric 1xATR14 stop, 1R target and 10h hold. Diff -0.007R, CI [-0.031, +0.019]. Powered NULL (MDE 0.035): the direction of the SMT does not predict the next move.
Same book as reading a, but only SMTs whose sweeping asset closes back beyond the swept level (a reversal closure). Diff -0.025R, CI [-0.056, +0.006]. Powered NULL, leaning negative.

Reading a (SMT only at structural extremes): 1h CISD trades whose extreme took gold's PDH/PDL (1,840). Gate: XAG failed to take its own PDH/PDL by the confirm bar; it fired on 27%. Diff +0.05R, CI [-0.057, +0.161], MDE 0.156, so UNDERPOWERED.

Reading b (SMT at any scale, intra-range): all 8,034 1h CISD trades. Gate: 1h gold/XAG SMT at the nearest 2/2 swing within 20 bars of the extreme; it fired on 31%. Diff +0.000R, CI [-0.054, +0.054]. Powered NULL (MDE 0.077).

Gold and XAG both print a same-direction 1h FVG on the same bar. Within 20 bars exactly one of them trades into its gap's near edge, and gold is traded away from the gap (1xATR stop, 1R, 10h). Diff +0.030R, CI [-0.009, +0.065]. Powered NULL (MDE 0.053).

Claim '-': the level gold held in a silver-swept SMT should break less often than chance. It breaks within 600 M1 bars 61.1% of the time, against 59.7% for a same-distance null. Diff +1.4pp (the wrong sign), CI [-0.3, +3.2]pp.

Baseline: every hourly SMT traded directly (1xATR stop, 1R, 10h), 7,136 events. Gate: a same-direction 1h CISD (the model) confirmed within the 3h before the SMT; it fires on 20%. Model-first minus SMT-first is +0.021R, CI [-0.048, +0.092]. MDE 0.1002 against the 0.10 threshold, so UNDERPOWERED by a hair.

Reversal SMT (XAU/EUR or XAU/GBP failed to take its C1 extreme on the C2 hour) used as a gate on the 1h small-wick C2 reversal book (2R, 10 bars): the SMT arm (44% of 7,520) was no better than the complement, powered NULL
Continuation SMT (exactly one of gold / gold-euro / gold-pound retook its C2 extreme during C3) used as a gate on the 1h sequential-C3 continuation book: +0.045R with the CI spanning 0, powered NULL

Tested the intraday substitution on 1h: gold makes a failure swing that does not sweep its last 2/2 swing low while silver sweeps its counterpart, then gold closes through the opposing-series open. Long with the stop on the unswept low, 2R, 10h. +0.065R, MDE 0.132, UNDERPOWERED.

Tested the daily C2 substitution: C2 days where gold takes the PDL and closes back inside, with the SMT gate (silver did not take its PDL) against C2 days without SMT, traded the next day. Gated n=246, MDE 0.30, UNDERPOWERED.

Refuted (both): with a ToD-matched control H2 turns negative; all of it is 2016-2021; the bare trigger earns ~40%.

Two-model trade. Sponsor: a live 4H FVG, which fails on a 4H close beyond its far edge. Execution: the first 5m CISD whose swing is inside the gap. Stop at that swing, target the most recent 4H swing (the sponsor's liquidity), hold 40h, one trade per array. Diff +0.034R, CI [-0.085, +0.154]; MDE 0.171.
Projection as target: 15m CISD entry, stop at the manipulation extreme, target the -2 projection of the leg from the origin swing to the extreme, 12h hold. NULL.

Band as reaction area: on the first touch of -2 (before the extreme is retaken, within 24h) trade the retracement, target -1, stop -4, against a matched control at the same geometry. A well-powered NULL (diff 0.000R).

15m CISD book, protected-swing stop where the extreme swept a prior intact 2/2 swing (20.6% of events) vs a fresh swing: -0.018R, a powered NULL, both halves slightly negative. Stops behind already-swept liquidity are not safer.

Stop at the protected-swing wick versus the body extreme of the opposing series, on the same 1h CISD entries at 2R. The wick stop was not better (-0.009R, CI [-0.048, +0.027]): a powered null. Only one reading was run, the channel's canonical wick vs body contrast.

Reading A: a limit at the order block's mean threshold (live 3h, cancelled if the 2R objective trades first), same structural stop, 2R. Compared with a market entry on the same 1h CISD. There was no difference (+0.005R, CI [-0.053, +0.067]): a powered null.
Reading B (keep the stop, cut position size) is untestable: it is sizing arithmetic. It changes dollars per trade, not R, so it is identical to the baseline in any R-based test.

Pooled the five spoken 1h STRAT reversals (2-2, 1-2-2, 3-2-2, 2-1-2, 3-1-2), entered on the M1 trigger through the prior bar's extreme with day-candle timeframe continuity. Target = opposite extreme of the bar before P, stop = other side of P, 10h hold. Result -0.003R vs control, powered (MDE 0.023), so NULL.
The taxonomy is definitional, so only 'a 2 is trending' was scored. Trade every closed 1h 2 in its direction, stop at its opposite extreme, 1R, 10h hold. Result +0.003R, CI [-0.007, +0.014].

Daily inside bar, traded on the next day's first M1 break. Target the mother bar's extreme, stop the inside bar's far side, one-day hold on bars. Result +0.054R vs control, CI [-0.010, +0.120]. Powered (MDE 0.093), so NULL.

Weekly outside bar: last week's high or low taken on Monday or Tuesday, then a counter 1h CISD. Target the other side of last week, stop the week's extreme, hold to the week's close. Result -0.09R, CI [-0.33, +0.17]. Only 160 weeks, so underpowered. Re-run on hold_basis=bars per trap 7.

Daily inside-bar breakouts that closed beyond the inside bar, targeting the nearest untaken high/low among the 10 prior candles within 5 sessions. Hit rate 72.3% vs geometry-matched null 76.6%. Only 119 events and MDE 0.124, so UNDERPOWERED.

Live reading on 5m bare CISD: the in-progress hour is a 2 in the trade's direction, against hours that are a 1 (inside). The gated trades did 0.044R worse, [-0.061, -0.027], and both halves are negative. Waiting for the hour to be a 2 means buying after the extension.
Confirmed-at-close reading: the last completed hour is a 2 in the trade's direction, against a 1. Result -0.012R [-0.035, +0.010]. Powered NULL.

Gate on the 4h CISD rung-0 book (forex grid, 2R, 40h hold on bars): does the trade agree with the monthly candle's side of its open? With-continuity trades did worse, -0.078R, CI [-0.183, +0.029]. MDE 0.152, so underpowered.

Trade test. 15m setup: sweep, then a close through structure, then an FVG, then a tap of the FVG. Trigger: a 5m Strat break of the previous 5m candle's extreme; stop at the trigger candles' extreme, 2R, 50 min. Result -0.005R [-0.053, +0.046]: powered NULL (MDE 0.071).

15m 2-2 reversals (stop at the 2down/2up extreme, 2R), gated on a preceding liquidity run (the reversal bar first undercuts the latest confirmed 2/2 swing). Gated vs ungated -0.009R, powered NULL. Side note: the ungated complement beat its own control by +0.027R (p=2e-5), which is not what the concept claims.
5m bare CISD on days whose prior daily candle was a C2/C3 closure. Gate = the CISD agrees with that daily closure's direction. Powered NULL (+0.001R).

5m bare CISD whose close sits inside an opposing, still-open 1h FVG (the 'retracement into an HTF PD array' reading), claim '-'. Point estimate -0.023R, in the claimed direction, but the CI includes 0. Powered NULL.
Gate on the 1h CISD book: allowed only once the current trading day has taken the previous day's high or low (a daily Strat '1' is not yet resolved). -0.003R [-0.058, +0.050], NULL and powered.

No-trade rule tested as a gate (claim '-') on the rung-0 1h CISD book. Stuck = price between an active bullish daily FVG below and an active bearish daily FVG above. Stuck trades did not do worse (+0.020R). Powered NULL.

Resolution trigger tested as a trade: a daily close through the upper or lower array after a stuck state, entered at the next open with the stop at the array's far side, 2R, 120h hold. Only 148 trades, MDE 0.31: UNDERPOWERED.
Gate on the 15m bare CISD: does the strict trigger also clear the whole-move level (the 'ignore small candles, take the whole move' reading)? The gate passed on 87% of triggers. Powered NULL.
Gate on the 15m bare CISD: does the first candle of the opposing series form a strict 3-bar swing (the 'skip a non-swing candle' reading)? Powered NULL.

1h: every strict 3-bar swing traded as a reversal at its confirmation, stop at the swing extreme, 2R, 10h. diff about 0. Labelled UNDERPOWERED rather than NULL because 23% of control draws overlap the concept's own trades (the r2 attenuation rule).
1h: only 'genuine' swings, i.e. those that take out the last confirmed same-side swing, traded as reversals. Powered NULL (+0.017R).

Book: first-touch 1h FVG entries (stop at the far edge, 2R). Gate: a confirmed 1h swing point within 0.5 ATR just outside the gap, swept by the touch, against isolated gaps. Diff +0.049R, MDE 0.20: UNDERPOWERED.

Gate on the 5m bare-CISD baseline (98,346 trades, 2R, 50 min hold). Gate: the CISD extreme ran a 3-candle 5m swing (within 12 bars) into an unfilled 1H FVG (within 24h); it fired on 10.5%. Gated minus complement = +0.020R, CI [-0.003, +0.045]. Powered NULL (MDE 0.034).

T-spot read as the C2 equilibrium (4h C2 with a 15m CISD). The rate at which C3 trades beyond the equilibrium is 63.4%, against 62.7% for a matched null (same distance and bars). Diff +0.006 [-0.010, +0.023]. Powered null.

T-spot read as the overlap of 0.5 of the C2 wick and 0.5 of the CISD series bodies, using the band's deeper edge. C3 trades beyond it 44.2% of the time, against 45.3% for the matched null. Diff -0.011 [-0.027, +0.005]. Powered null.

Scored the post-T1 runner leg of 1h CISD trades that reached T1 before the stop: stop moved to break-even at entry, T2 = prior-day high/low beyond T1, 10h hold. Vs a matched random control: +0.032R [-0.071, +0.132]. MDE 0.145 misses the 0.10 threshold, so UNDERPOWERED.

After a 1H CISD reversal: is the nearest untaken consolidation low (4 bars within 1 ATR, inside a 72-bar leg) reached within one session? Hit rate 47.9% vs geometry-matched null 49.3%. Powered NULL (MDE 0.035).
5m relatively-equal highs/lows (within 0.10 ATR, 48 bars) are reached within 240 M1 bars 77.7% of the time vs 77.1% for an ATR-scaled distance-matched null. Powered NULL.
Refuted (faithfulness): non-FVG bars with matched geometry show almost the same lift - it is 'revisit the last bar's extreme'.

The 10:00 deadline (claim '-'): when the 9:30 objective (nearer untaken previous-day extreme) is still unmet at 10:00, is it reached less often in 10:00-12:00 than a null at the same distance at 10:00 on another day? 8.0% vs 8.1%. Retracement at the 4H flip after an expansion candle (futures grid 22/02/06/10/14, the 18:00 flip excluded). Hit = price returns to the prior body's midpoint within 60 M1 bars; the null uses the same distance at the same NY clock on other days. 33.7% vs 35.5%;

The +0.55R on n=17 means nothing.

Thursday-reversal reading: Thursday is a counter daily C2 with an hourly CISD, short at the Friday open with a 25% retracement target. 72 events, but 54 had already reached the target by Thursday's close, leaving 18 trades. Below n=30, so UNTESTABLE.

The three-way taxonomy is exhaustive by construction, so the test is of its use: are PDH and PDL the likely draws? The next session touches PDH or PDL 84.7% of the time, against 86.4% for levels at the same distances from random matched times.

Gate on the 1h CISD book: block trades in the direction of a run of three or more same-direction daily candle bodies (11% blocked). +0.062R [-0.023, +0.150]. MDE 0.124, so UNDERPOWERED; the sign agrees with the claim.

An expansion is 'anticipated' when daily order flow (daily closes against daily FVGs) is established and no consolidation trigger fires. The next day expands in that direction (body >= 0.5 ADR20) 21.5% of the time vs a 20.5% same-direction base rate within +/-30 days: +1.0pp, CI [-1.4, +3.4]pp. Powered, so NULL.

Reversal entry after the third close-back drive through the same 1h swing level (within 0.5 ATR), stop at the drives' extreme, 2R. Result -0.21R against the matched control, CI excludes 0 against the claim: NEGATIVE, p=0.03, small n. It is only a candidate until the multiplicity correction.

Third drive against first and second drives on the same levels, all 7,477 drive entries, clustered by level. The third drive does worse (-0.18R): borderline NEGATIVE. Its trades are the same ones as reading a, so the two readings are not independent.

Gate test on the phase-3 15m CISD book. The gated arm meets at least 2 of the 3 criteria: PDH/PDL not yet taken, under half of the 5-day mean range used, entry within 0.25 of that range from the 18:00 open. Result +0.021R [-0.007, +0.046] against the 12,911 trades scoring 0 or 1. Powered, so NULL.

Gate on the GB 0.7475 book: three or more arrays (level + unmitigated 15m/1h FVG, order block, 50% of the extreme wick) overlapping the 0.705-0.79 zone vs fewer. Fired on 594 of 6970 fills (8.5%). Result −0.068R, wrong sign, and UNDERPOWERED (MDE 0.155).

Friday branch: Tue and Wed expand with no internal swing, then Thursday prints a daily C2 plus an hourly CISD; trade Friday toward the weekly open with the stop beyond Thursday's extreme. Only 35 weeks qualify, so the test is underpowered.

Thursday-intraday branch: enter at the first hourly CISD after Wednesday's extreme is swept, target the weekly open, hold to Friday's close. n=52, underpowered. Re-run once with hold_basis=bars per trap 7 because clock-run exposure differed by 18%.

At 2h into each forex-grid 4H candle whose running candle has a small wick (opp/body<=1.0), trade its direction with stop at the running extreme and hold to the 4H close (clock-matched control). The CI contains 0 (MDE 0.036), but 33% of control draws overlap real trades, so NULL is downgraded to UNDERPOWERED.

9:30 expansion ride: the 09:30 15m candle is a small-wick expansion candle (ratio <= 1.0). Enter at 09:45 in its direction, stop at its opposing extreme, target the untaken previous-day extreme, exit at 10:00; clock-fixed controls. Powered NULL, -0.021R.
Variant book: the same 9:30-expansion entries exited at 10:00 vs held to 12:00, with the same stop and target. +0.013R for the 10:00 exit, CI [-0.089, +0.107]. UNDERPOWERED (MDE 0.14).
Baseline is the phase-3 rung-0 15m CISD. Gate: the in-progress 1D, 4H and 1H candles all support the trade by wick geometry (price beyond the open and opposing run <= body so far). NULL, powered.

Same 15m CISD baseline. Gate: 'all timeframes green', meaning price is beyond the open of the in-progress 1D, 4H and 1H candles in the trade direction. NULL, powered; the point estimate is +0.024R and the CI just touches 0.

Tag of the previous HTF bar's high or low, confirmed by a CISD on the LTF. Gate on the bare 5m CISD book: the last completed 1H candle is a C2 or C3 (reading A) closure in the entry's direction (the 1H -> 5m pair). Result: -0.010R, a powered null (MDE 0.025).
Same test on the 4H (forex grid) -> 15m pair. Result: -0.006R, a powered null (MDE 0.043).

Gate on the phase-3 1h CISD book: month, week and day all coloured live in the trade's direction, and none of them an inside bar. The gate fired on 11% of trades (880). The difference was -0.03R with the CI spanning zero. MDE 0.114 exceeds 0.10, so the result is UNDERPOWERED.

Gate on the phase-3 5m CISD book, 50-minute hold. It compares signals decided after the 60m has decoupled from the 18:00 NY day open with those in the first hour (18:00-19:00, about 4.6% of trades). Powered NULL (MDE 0.049). Caveat: the first hour is also the post-halt reopen period.
Alignment reading: a 5m CISD is gated when its direction matches the latest 1h CISD. Result +0.013R, CI contains 0, powered NULL (MDE 0.023).
HTF-level reading: a 5m CISD is gated only after price has traded through the prior 1h bar's low or high within the last 60 min. Result: powered NULL.
Gate on the 5m CISD entry book: the entry direction agrees with the daily bias from the previous-candle engine on the last completed day. Result: +0.005R, a powered null (MDE 0.025).

Full Daily -> 1H -> 5m ladder: the daily bias agrees with the entry and the 5m setup's swept extreme took out the previous completed 1H candle's low or high (the hourly POI). Result: +0.015R, a powered null (MDE 0.031).

Book: rung-0 15m CISD. Gate: the turn's extreme swept the most recent confirmed 1h swing (manipulation) against a turn that left it intact (failure swing). Swept turns do slightly worse (-0.030R): borderline NEGATIVE, powered.

4h rung-0 CISD book (~3.9 signals a week, near his cadence), first two signals of the week vs the 3rd and later: +0.031R, MDE 0.14 > 0.10, so UNDERPOWERED; the halves disagree. Powered (MDE 0.034). The 'ranging morning -> downgrade' clause is not quantified in the corpus and was not tested.
Refuted (both): an unusually bad locked-seed control draw (3.8 SD) and block B2 only; the independent build is NULL.

30m rung-0 CISD with the stop at 50% of the opposing-candle series and a 2R target vs a matched random control: +0.001R, a powered zero. Price does not respect the half level more than random.

Mechanical trail events inside open 15m CISD positions (stop moved to each new opposing candle's extreme, clustered by parent) vs a random stop at the same distance: -0.015R, NULL. The trailed levels do not hold better than random ones.

Trend = 2 consecutive days taking PDH (or PDL) by wick. Hit = the next session takes today's high (low); null = same distance and same bar horizon from random moments. 50.7% vs null 54.9%, so the trend-conditioned draw is hit LESS often than geometry predicts.
Refuted (both): reduces to the cheat-code first opposing candle; the whole effect is in the smallest-stop quintile (median stop 0.11pt).

Daily C2 bias, a same-direction 4h C2 (forex grid), then the first 15m CISD inside 4h C3 holding the C2 half; 2R, 150 min. -0.022R, CI [-0.169,+0.128]. Underpowered, and the sign agrees with phase 3's -0.028R.

Full playbook: a daily C2/C3 closure confirmed by an hourly CISD, then an hourly C2 in the previous day's bias-side half, then a 5m CISD within the next hour; 2R target, 50-minute hold. The difference is negative and underpowered (MDE 0.119), consistent with phase 3's refuted 5m/1H/1D conjunction.

Bias from a 1H C2/C3 closure, then a 15m C2 that forms the next hour's wick, entered at the 15m close with a stop at the swing, 2R target, 60-minute hold. +0.010R against the matched control, powered NULL (MDE 0.036).

Weekly C2 bias, then a daily C2 plus a 1H CISD in that direction, entered at the daily close with a stop at the daily extreme, target the weekly draw (only if at least 2R away), exit at the week close. Only 41 trades in 10.5 years, so UNDERPOWERED.

Same 1H gold/silver SMT book. Gate 'stage2' (38% of trades): on the next bar either a PSP (opposite-colour closes) or a candle-2/candle-3 SMT. Two-stage minus one-stage = +0.004R, CI [-0.061, +0.069], powered (MDE 0.093), so NULL: the second stage adds nothing.

Gate on the 5m unicorn limit book: breaker L1->H1->lower low->close through H1, with an overlapping same-direction FVG. Limit at the overlap edge, stop at the breaker's far edge, 2R, 50 min hold. Gated = formation count from L1 to completion <= 12 bars (3,462) vs 13-48 bars (4,758).

The pattern alone on 5m (breaker plus overlapping FVG, limit at the overlap edge, stop at the swept extreme, 2R). A powered zero against the matched control.
The same unicorn restricted to setups confirmed at a session open (London 02:00-05:00, NY 09:30-11:00). A powered zero.

Close reading on the same book. Gate: no 1h close of the day beyond the previous day's EQ, against the trade (fires 61.9%). -0.027R, CI [-0.103, +0.053], MDE 0.112.

Baseline is the 1h CISD book targeting the untaken prior-day high/low, 10h hold. Gate: entry sits in the swing-side half of the swing-to-target distance, which fired on 66.9% of events. Gated vs complement: +0.018R [-0.041, +0.076]. Powered null (MDE 0.084).
